name: Golden Hour
definition: The warm, honey-colored light you get just after sunrise or before sunset. It makes everything look softer, kinder, and more expensive.
when_to_use: Use when you want instant warmth and beauty with one word. If a prompt feels flat, this is the first thing to try.
prompt_example: "portrait of a gardener, golden hour light"

name: Rim Light
definition: A thin outline of light around your subject's edges, like they're glowing from behind. Separates the subject from the background beautifully.
when_to_use: Use when your subject blends into the background, or you want a cinematic, polished feel.
prompt_example: "black cat on a fence, rim light, dusk"

name: Chiaroscuro
definition: An old painting term for dramatic light against deep shadow. Think candlelit faces in dark rooms, Rembrandt style.
when_to_use: Use for moody portraits, mystery, and drama. Not for cheerful scenes; it will darken everything.
prompt_example: "violinist in an empty theatre, chiaroscuro"

name: Overcast Light
definition: The soft, even light of a cloudy day. No harsh shadows, no squinting. Very flattering and calm.
when_to_use: Use for gentle, honest scenes and soft product shots. Great when harsh shadows keep ruining your image.
prompt_example: "woman reading on a porch, overcast light"

name: Neon Glow
definition: Electric, colorful light like city signs at night. Pinks, blues, and purples bouncing off wet streets and faces.
when_to_use: Use for nightlife, retro-future vibes, or anything that should feel electric and modern.
prompt_example: "ramen stall at midnight, neon glow"

name: Candlelight
definition: Warm, flickering, intimate light from a small flame. Everything feels closer and quieter.
when_to_use: Use for cozy, romantic, or historical scenes. It naturally darkens the edges of the frame.
prompt_example: "handwritten letter on a desk, candlelight"

name: Volumetric Light
definition: Light you can see traveling through the air, like sunbeams through dust or fog. Adds instant atmosphere and depth.
when_to_use: Use when a scene feels empty; visible light rays fill space beautifully. Forests, churches, and windows love this.
prompt_example: "old library, volumetric light through tall windows"

name: Bioluminescence
definition: Natural glow from living things, like glowing mushrooms, plankton, or deep-sea creatures. Magical and otherworldly.
when_to_use: Use for fantasy scenes, night nature, and anything that should feel softly magical without being cartoonish.
prompt_example: "midnight forest floor, bioluminescent mushrooms"

name: Weathered
definition: Aged by time and the elements. Peeling paint, worn wood, soft rust. Surfaces that have lived a life.
when_to_use: Use to add character and honesty to objects and places. New and shiny often reads as fake; weathered reads as real.
prompt_example: "weathered fishing boat on a grey beach"

name: Iridescent
definition: A surface that shifts colors as it catches light, like soap bubbles, beetle shells, or oil on water.
when_to_use: Use for magic, luxury, and dreamlike surfaces. A little goes a long way.
prompt_example: "iridescent silk gown, studio light"

name: Velvet
definition: Deep, soft, light-absorbing fabric texture. Rich and touchable, with gentle sheen on the folds.
when_to_use: Use for luxury, warmth, and depth, especially in dark and moody scenes.
prompt_example: "emerald velvet armchair in a dim study"

name: Cracked Porcelain
definition: Fine, delicate cracks across a smooth ceramic surface, like an antique teacup. Fragile beauty.
when_to_use: Use for elegance with a hint of sadness or age. Beautiful on faces in surreal art.
prompt_example: "porcelain doll face with fine cracks, soft light"

name: Brushed Metal
definition: Metal with a fine, satiny grain instead of a mirror shine. Modern, clean, industrial.
when_to_use: Use for product shots, tech, and modern interiors when chrome feels too flashy.
prompt_example: "brushed metal coffee machine, morning kitchen light"

name: Moss Covered
definition: Soft green growth blanketing stone, wood, or forgotten things. Nature quietly taking over.
when_to_use: Use for enchanted forests, ruins, and anything that should feel ancient and alive.
prompt_example: "moss covered stone stairway into a forest"

name: Watercolor
definition: Soft, translucent paint that bleeds and blooms on paper. Edges melt; colors breathe.
when_to_use: Use for gentle, emotional, storybook feels. Terrible for sharp detail; wonderful for mood.
prompt_example: "watercolor painting of a rainy street market"

name: Oil Painting
definition: Rich, layered classical paint with visible brushwork and deep color. The museum look.
when_to_use: Use for portraits, drama, and timelessness. Instantly makes a scene feel important.
prompt_example: "oil painting of a woman with pink hair, dark background"

name: Papercraft
definition: Scenes built from cut, folded, and layered paper. Handmade, dimensional, and charming.
when_to_use: Use for playful explainers, craft aesthetics, and gentle 3D without computer-render coldness.
prompt_example: "papercraft diorama of a lighthouse in a storm"

name: Claymation
definition: The look of hand-molded clay characters, with fingerprint softness and stop-motion charm.
when_to_use: Use for friendly characters and nostalgic, handmade animation vibes.
prompt_example: "claymation robot watering a tiny garden"

name: Charcoal Sketch
definition: Loose, smudgy black drawing with rough strokes and soft shading. Raw and expressive.
when_to_use: Use for emotion, movement studies, and dramatic portraits where polish would kill the feeling.
prompt_example: "charcoal sketch of a dancer mid-leap"

name: Stained Glass
definition: Bold shapes outlined in dark lead, filled with glowing colored glass. Light becomes the artwork.
when_to_use: Use for spiritual, ornate, or fairytale imagery. Strong silhouettes work best.
prompt_example: "stained glass window of a fox in a moonlit forest"

name: Fog
definition: Thick soft mist that hides distance and mutes color. The world becomes quiet and mysterious.
when_to_use: Use to simplify busy scenes, add mystery, or make light rays visible.
prompt_example: "lone streetlamp in heavy fog"

name: Golden Autumn
definition: Peak fall: amber leaves, low warm sun, long shadows. Cozy and a little nostalgic.
when_to_use: Use for warmth, harvest scenes, and gentle melancholy.
prompt_example: "golden autumn park, falling leaves, long shadows"

name: Monsoon Rain
definition: Heavy, dramatic, warm rain. Sheets of water, glossy streets, life carrying on under umbrellas.
when_to_use: Use for drama and atmosphere in city or tropical scenes. Reflections double the beauty.
prompt_example: "market street in monsoon rain, umbrellas glowing"

name: First Snow
definition: Light, fresh snowfall that hasn't been walked through yet. Clean, quiet, hopeful.
when_to_use: Use for winter softness without harshness, and for scenes about new beginnings.
prompt_example: "red postbox under first snow, early morning"

name: Heat Haze
definition: The shimmery, wavy air above hot roads and deserts. You can feel the temperature.
when_to_use: Use for deserts, summer roads, and tension. It adds motion to still scenes.
prompt_example: "empty desert highway, heat haze on the horizon"

name: Dreamscape
definition: A landscape built from dream logic: floating islands, impossible skies, soft physics.
when_to_use: Use when reality is optional. Great for surreal art and emotional storytelling.
prompt_example: "pastel dreamscape with floating staircases and slow clouds"

name: Cityscape
definition: A wide view of a city: rooftops, lights, layers of buildings stacked to the horizon.
when_to_use: Use for establishing shots, urban energy, and scale.
prompt_example: "rainy cityscape at blue hour, glowing windows"

name: Seascape
definition: The ocean as the subject: waves, horizon, weather, and light on water.
when_to_use: Use for calm, power, or loneliness. The mood of the water is the mood of the image.
prompt_example: "stormy seascape with a distant lighthouse"

name: Microscape
definition: A tiny world shot like a landscape: moss becomes forest, dew becomes lakes.
when_to_use: Use for wonder and fresh perspective. Familiar things become magical at ant scale.
prompt_example: "microscape of a mossy log, dew drops like ponds"

name: Cloudscape
definition: The sky as the whole scene: towering clouds, light beams, endless space.
when_to_use: Use for freedom, spirituality, and scale. Beautiful backdrop for flying subjects.
prompt_example: "golden cloudscape at sunset, birds crossing"

name: Art Deco Era
definition: The glamorous 1920s-30s look: geometric patterns, gold and black, luxury and symmetry.
when_to_use: Use for elegance, posters, architecture, and Gatsby-flavored glamour.
prompt_example: "art deco hotel lobby, gold and black, symmetrical"

name: Victorian Era
definition: The 1800s look: ornate detail, dark wood, lace, gas lamps, and formality with secrets.
when_to_use: Use for gothic romance, period portraits, and moody interiors.
prompt_example: "victorian era study, gas lamp, leather books"

name: Retro 70s
definition: Warm oranges and browns, funky patterns, film grain, and sun-faded optimism.
when_to_use: Use for nostalgia, music culture, and warm analog vibes.
prompt_example: "retro 70s kitchen, orange tones, film grain"

name: Y2K
definition: Late 90s to early 2000s: glossy plastic, chrome, bubble shapes, digital optimism.
when_to_use: Use for playful nostalgia and fashion-forward content aimed at millennial memory lanes.
prompt_example: "y2k desktop setup, translucent plastic, chrome accents"

name: Jewel Tones
definition: Deep, saturated colors named after gems: emerald, ruby, sapphire, amethyst. Rich and confident.
when_to_use: Use for luxury, drama, and depth. They love dark backgrounds and velvet textures.
prompt_example: "portrait in jewel tones, emerald background"

name: Pastel Palette
definition: Soft, milky, gentle colors: baby pink, mint, lavender, cream. Sweet and calming.
when_to_use: Use for gentle, dreamy, friendly content. The default palette of soft aesthetics.
prompt_example: "pastel palette bakery storefront, morning light"

name: Muted Palette
definition: Colors with the volume turned down: dusty, greyed, quiet tones. Sophisticated and calm.
when_to_use: Use when bright colors feel cheap or loud. Editorial and interior content loves this.
prompt_example: "muted palette living room, linen and clay tones"

name: Teal and Orange
definition: The classic movie color combo: warm skin tones against cool teal shadows. Instantly cinematic.
when_to_use: Use for cinematic stills and action scenes. It is the fastest route to a film look.
prompt_example: "teal and orange street scene, cinematic still"

name: Macro Photography
definition: Extreme close-up photography where tiny things fill the frame: insect eyes, dew drops, fabric weave.
when_to_use: Use for detail, texture, and wonder. Backgrounds melt into soft blur automatically.
prompt_example: "macro photography of frost on a leaf"

name: Long Exposure
definition: A slow camera that turns motion into smooth streaks: silky waterfalls, light trails, ghost crowds.
when_to_use: Use for movement, time, and calm. Water and traffic become magic.
prompt_example: "long exposure waterfall in a dark forest"

name: Candid
definition: Unposed, caught-in-the-moment photography. Real expressions, imperfect framing, honest life.
when_to_use: Use when posed images feel stiff. Perfect for storytelling and documentary feels.
prompt_example: "candid photo of friends laughing at a kitchen table"

name: Editorial
definition: Magazine-style photography: intentional, styled, confident. Every element placed on purpose.
when_to_use: Use for fashion, products, and brand imagery that should feel premium.
prompt_example: "editorial photo of a woman in a structured coat, studio"

name: Film Photography
definition: The analog look: gentle grain, imperfect color, soft highlights. Warmth digital can't fake.
when_to_use: Use for nostalgia and humanity. Makes AI images feel less AI.
prompt_example: "film photography of a seaside town, slight grain"

name: Ethereal
definition: Light, airy, and not quite of this world. Glow, softness, and a floating feeling.
when_to_use: Use to lift any scene toward the magical. One of the strongest single-word mood shifters.
prompt_example: "ethereal portrait, soft glow, floating fabric"

name: Ominous
definition: Something bad is coming. Heavy skies, long shadows, and quiet tension.
when_to_use: Use for thrillers, storms, and drama. It darkens mood without adding gore.
prompt_example: "ominous farmhouse under a green storm sky"

name: Opulent
definition: Extreme, unapologetic luxury. Gold, marble, abundance stacked on abundance.
when_to_use: Use for wealth, fantasy palaces, and maximalist beauty.
prompt_example: "opulent banquet table, gold candelabras, marble hall"

name: Serene
definition: Deep calm. Still water, soft light, nothing rushing anywhere.
when_to_use: Use for wellness, nature, and breathing room. The antidote to busy images.
prompt_example: "serene mountain lake at dawn, mist rising"

name: Biopunk Rococo
definition: Ornate 18th-century curls and gilding grown from living tissue, vines, and organic machinery. Lavish and unsettling in the best way.
when_to_use: Use for high-concept fantasy, album art, and scenes where beauty should feel slightly alive.
prompt_example: "biopunk rococo throne room, living gold filigree"

name: Ukiyo-e Vaporwave
definition: Classic Japanese woodblock composition dressed in neon pinks, teals, and retro-digital sunset gradients.
when_to_use: Use for striking wall art and content that bridges traditional and internet aesthetics.
prompt_example: "ukiyo-e vaporwave great wave, neon sunset grid"

name: Brutalist Botanical
definition: Massive raw concrete forms softened by wild, overflowing plant life. Cold architecture, warm nature, perfect tension.
when_to_use: Use for architecture content, book covers, and solarpunk-adjacent worldbuilding.
prompt_example: "brutalist botanical tower, concrete and hanging gardens"

name: Gothic Kawaii
definition: Cute meets creepy: pastel bats, smiling ghosts, lace and skulls in candy colors. Wednesday Addams meets Lisa Frank.
when_to_use: Use for playful dark content, stickers, and brand imagery with bite.
prompt_example: "gothic kawaii ghost tea party, pastel and black lace"

name: Kawaii Gamer
definition: Cute-culture meets gaming setup: pastel peripherals, plushies, RGB glow softened into candy colors.
when_to_use: Use for cozy tech scenes, streamer aesthetics, or anything that should feel playful and plugged-in.
prompt_example: "desk setup, kawaii gamer aesthetic, pastel pink"

name: Emo
definition: Early-2000s mall goth mood: black layers, side-swept fringe, checkerboard, eyeliner, and feelings.
when_to_use: Use for nostalgic 2000s portraits or moody youth-culture scenes with a soft heart.
prompt_example: "portrait of a teenager, emo aesthetic, 2005"

name: Grunge
definition: Worn, layered, deliberately undone: flannel, ripped denim, faded film texture, a little grime.
when_to_use: Use to rough up a scene that feels too clean or add 90s attitude.
prompt_example: "street portrait, grunge aesthetic, 35mm film"

name: Fairy Grunge
definition: Woodland whimsy dragged through the mud: fairy wings and lace with dirt, moss, and distressed layers.
when_to_use: Use when you want magic that looks lived-in rather than polished.
prompt_example: "forest wanderer, fairy grunge aesthetic"

name: Fairy Academia
definition: Dark academia's bookish charm with mushrooms, moth wings, and forest-library light.
when_to_use: Use for scholarly-magical scenes: old books, candlelight, and something watching from the ferns.
prompt_example: "reading nook in a hollow tree, fairy academia"

name: Dual Kawaii
definition: Split-personality cute: one half sweet pastels, the other half dark or edgy, in a single design.
when_to_use: Use for character designs that need contrast or before-and-after energy in one frame.
prompt_example: "character sheet, dual kawaii style, half pastel half black"

name: Dolly Kei
definition: Japanese street fashion built from antique European dolls: layered vintage fabrics, religious motifs, dark fairy-tale trims.
when_to_use: Use for richly layered vintage fashion portraits with a storybook shadow.
prompt_example: "fashion portrait, dolly kei style"

name: Soft Macabre
definition: Death and decay rendered gently: skulls in pastel, ghosts that look huggable.
when_to_use: Use for spooky subjects that should charm rather than frighten.
prompt_example: "still life with skull and roses, soft macabre"

name: Bubble Goth
definition: Goth cheerfulness: black-and-neon palettes, glossy textures, cute darkness invented by pop artist Kerli.
when_to_use: Use when gothic subjects need bounce, shine, and a bit of bubblegum.
prompt_example: "portrait, bubble goth aesthetic, pastel and black"

name: Pixiecore
definition: Small winged mischief: glitter, petals, dewdrops, and light that looks freshly enchanted.
when_to_use: Use for delicate magical scenes with a playful rather than grand tone.
prompt_example: "tiny pixie village in a teacup, pixiecore"

name: Pasta Art
definition: Artwork built from actual pasta shapes: macaroni mosaics, spaghetti linework, farfalle flourishes.
when_to_use: Use for playful food art, craft-project textures, or delightfully absurd portraits.
prompt_example: "portrait of a cat made of pasta, pasta art"

name: Synchromism
definition: Early abstract movement painting with color the way composers use chords: rhythmic, swirling color harmonies.
when_to_use: Use for abstract pieces where color itself is the subject.
prompt_example: "abstract composition, synchromism style"

name: Neo Gothic
definition: Gothic architecture and mood revived with modern drama: pointed arches, tracery, contemporary darkness.
when_to_use: Use for architecture, interiors, or portraits that need cathedral-scale atmosphere.
prompt_example: "cathedral interior, neo gothic style"

name: Hard Edge Painting
definition: Crisp geometric color fields with razor-clean boundaries; no brushwork, no blending.
when_to_use: Use for bold graphic compositions and modernist poster energy.
prompt_example: "abstract composition, hard edge painting"

name: Cybergoth
definition: Goth fused with rave tech: black PVC, neon dreads, goggles, industrial club lighting.
when_to_use: Use for futuristic club scenes or characters equal parts dark and glowing.
prompt_example: "dancer portrait, cybergoth style, neon green"

name: Art Povera
definition: Italian movement making art from humble materials: rags, soil, rope, found scraps as fine art.
when_to_use: Use for textured, materials-first compositions that feel honest and raw.
prompt_example: "sculpture of a horse, arte povera style"

name: Concrete Art
definition: Pure geometric abstraction with no reference to the real world; math made visual.
when_to_use: Use for clean, rational abstract pieces and modernist design work.
prompt_example: "geometric abstract, concrete art style"

name: Post-modernism
definition: Rule-breaking mashup of styles, eras, and irony; high art and pop culture in the same frame.
when_to_use: Use when you want deliberate stylistic collision and a wink.
prompt_example: "living room interior, postmodernism, 1980s"

name: Avant-Pop Surrealism
definition: Pop-culture imagery bent into dream logic: glossy, strange, and saturated.
when_to_use: Use for editorial-weird portraits and album-cover energy.
prompt_example: "portrait with melting television, avant-pop surrealism"

name: Abstract Futuristic
definition: Sleek non-representational forms suggesting speed, tech, and tomorrow: chrome curves and light trails.
when_to_use: Use for backgrounds, branding, and tech-forward abstract pieces.
prompt_example: "abstract futuristic composition, chrome and light"

name: Angura Kei
definition: Japanese underground theatre fashion: dark vintage kimono elements, dramatic makeup, Showa-era shadow.
when_to_use: Use for theatrical dark-fashion portraits with Japanese vintage roots.
prompt_example: "stage portrait, angura kei style"

name: Afrovictorian
definition: Victorian silhouettes and tailoring celebrated through African fabrics, patterns, and presence.
when_to_use: Use for regal historical-fusion portraits rich in pattern and dignity.
prompt_example: "portrait of a duchess, afrovictorian style"

name: Antique Grunge
definition: Aged elegance gone beautifully to seed: peeling gilt, foxed paper, dusty velvet.
when_to_use: Use for interiors and still lifes that should feel abandoned but grand.
prompt_example: "abandoned ballroom, antique grunge"

name: Artificial Nature
definition: Nature rebuilt synthetically: plastic flowers, LED forests, lab-grown landscapes.
when_to_use: Use for uncanny eco-futurist scenes questioning what counts as natural.
prompt_example: "garden of plastic flowers, artificial nature"

name: Abstract Tech

when_to_use: Use for tech-brand backgrounds and digital-native abstract art.

name: Anglo Gothic

when_to_use: Use for literary-gothic landscapes and portraits with British weather in their bones.
prompt_example: "manor on the moors, anglo gothic"

name: Romantic Academia
definition: Academia aesthetic warmed with poetry and longing: handwritten letters, roses on old books.
when_to_use: Use for soft scholarly scenes where the library is also a love story.

name: Pop Kei
definition: Japanese street fashion in maximum color: toy accessories, layered rainbow, deliberate sensory overload.
when_to_use: Use for joy-loud fashion portraits and candy-colored chaos.

name: Pixel Cutie

when_to_use: Use for approachable scholarly scenes without dark academia's gloom.

name: Party Kei
definition: Sparkly Japanese-inspired party fashion: sequins, tulle, plastic jewelry, celebration as a lifestyle.

name: Lens Flare
definition: Light strikes the lens directly, blooming into streaks and ghosts.
when_to_use: Use for sun-kissed warmth, sci-fi shine, or dreamy interruptions.
prompt_example: "backlit runner, warm lens flare crossing frame"

name: Bokeh
definition: Out-of-focus highlights rendered as soft glowing discs; blur as decoration.
when_to_use: Use for romantic night scenes and gentle backgrounds full of city lights.
prompt_example: "night portrait, street lamps as soft bokeh"

name: Rim Lighting
definition: Light from behind traces a bright edge around the subject, carving them from the dark.
when_to_use: Use for silhouettes with definition and heroic or mysterious outlines.
prompt_example: "boxer in the dark, rim lighting on his shoulders"

name: Low-Key Lighting
definition: Mostly shadow, sparse light, high contrast; noir's native language.
when_to_use: Use for mystery, dread, and moral ambiguity.
prompt_example: "interrogation room, low-key lighting, single lamp"

name: High-Key Lighting
definition: Bright, even, nearly shadowless illumination; open and optimistic.
when_to_use: Use for comedy, commercials, and worlds without secrets.
prompt_example: "morning kitchen scene, high-key lighting"

name: Practical Lighting
definition: Scenes lit by sources visible in frame: lamps, neon signs, candles, screens.
when_to_use: Use for naturalistic night interiors and cozy realism.
prompt_example: "bar scene lit only by practicals, neon and lamps"

name: Motivated Lighting
definition: Cinematic light that pretends to come from the scene's own sources, enhanced invisibly.
when_to_use: Use for polished realism where the lighting has an alibi.
prompt_example: "moonlight through blinds, motivated lighting"

name: Hard Light
definition: Small, direct sources casting crisp shadows and sharp texture; unforgiving and graphic.
when_to_use: Use for noir edges, desert sun, and faces with history.
prompt_example: "hard light across his face, blinds striping shadow"

name: Soft Key
definition: Large diffused main light wrapping gently around faces; flattering and calm.
when_to_use: Use for beauty work, interviews, and trustworthy warmth.
prompt_example: "soft key portrait, window light, gentle falloff"

name: Silhouette
definition: The subject reads as pure shape against a brighter background; identity through outline.
when_to_use: Use for mystery reveals, romantic dusk figures, and iconic frames.
prompt_example: "silhouette in the doorway, hallway blazing behind"

name: Match Cut
definition: Two shots joined by matching shape, motion, or idea; the edit itself tells a story.
when_to_use: Use for elegant time jumps and thematic rhymes between scenes.
prompt_example: "match cut from spinning coin to spinning ferris wheel"

name: Smash Cut
definition: An abrupt jarring cut between extremes: loud to silent, calm to chaos.
when_to_use: Use for shock, comedy, and waking from dreams badly.
prompt_example: "smash cut from the scream to the quiet breakfast table"

name: Cross Dissolve
definition: One image melts into the next; time passing with a soft edge.
when_to_use: Use for gentle time transitions and memory sequences.
prompt_example: "cross dissolve from her young face to the old photograph"

name: J-Cut
definition: The next scene's sound arrives before its picture; audio leads the way in.
when_to_use: Use for smooth scene flow and anticipation.
prompt_example: "J-cut: the crowd noise rises before we see the stadium"

name: L-Cut
definition: The previous scene's audio lingers over the new image; sound refuses to leave.
when_to_use: Use for reactions carrying into consequences and conversational flow.
prompt_example: "L-cut: her words continue over his face at the window"

name: Slow Motion
definition: Time stretched: motion rendered at high frame rate and played back slow, every detail savored.
when_to_use: Use for impact moments, beauty passes, and emotional peaks.
prompt_example: "slow motion, confetti falling around the champion"

name: Speed Ramp
definition: Footage accelerates or brakes mid-shot: real time snapping into slow motion and back.
when_to_use: Use for action emphasis and stylish energy shifts.
prompt_example: "speed ramp as the skater launches off the rail"

name: Bleach Bypass
definition: Desaturated, high-contrast silvery look from skipping the bleach step; war-film grit.
when_to_use: Use for harsh memories, conflict, and drained worlds.
prompt_example: "trench sequence, bleach bypass grade"

name: Day for Night
definition: Daylight footage graded into moonlight: cool, dim, and slightly unreal.
when_to_use: Use for stylized night scenes with dreamlike readability.
prompt_example: "day for night grade, silver-blue orchard"

name: Golden Hour Grade
definition: Warm amber light of the sun's first and last hour, honeyed and forgiving.
when_to_use: Use for romance, nostalgia, and endings that feel earned.
prompt_example: "golden hour grade, field at last light"
tags: beginner favorite;color;film look;gold;golden light;romantic;slow and emotional;video

name: 16mm Film Look
definition: Grainy, slightly soft small-gauge film texture; indie warmth and imperfection.
when_to_use: Use for memory sequences, music videos, and handmade honesty.
prompt_example: "16mm film look, summer lake, grain and halation"

name: Technicolor
definition: Vintage three-strip saturation: reds that sing, greens that glow, Hollywood's candy era.
when_to_use: Use for retro musicals, dream sequences, and joyful artifice.
prompt_example: "1950s kitchen, technicolor grade"

name: Noir Grade
definition: Deep blacks, silver highlights, venetian-blind shadows; crime cinema's monochrome soul.
when_to_use: Use for detective stories and moral shadow, color optional.
prompt_example: "office at night, noir grade, blinds shadow"
tags: black and white;color;dark colors;dramatic light;film look;moody;night;video

name: Neon Noir
definition: Noir updated in saturated neon: wet streets reflecting pink and cyan signage.
when_to_use: Use for modern night-city stories with electric melancholy.
prompt_example: "rain-slick alley, neon noir grade"

name: Pan
definition: The camera stays in one spot and turns left or right, like turning your head.
when_to_use: Use to follow someone across a room, or to reveal what is beside them.
prompt_example: "slow pan right across the busy market"

name: Truck Shot
definition: The whole camera slides sideways past the subject, so near and far things move at different speeds.
when_to_use: Use for smooth product glides and reveals with a real sense of depth.
prompt_example: "the camera trucks left past the coffee cup on the desk"

name: Arc Shot
definition: The camera curves part of the way around the subject.
when_to_use: Use to bring a still moment to life, or to show a new side of someone.
prompt_example: "slow arc around her as she reads the letter"

name: Pedestal
definition: The whole camera rises or lowers straight up and down, without tilting.
when_to_use: Use to rise above a scene and show its layout, or to drop down to eye level.
prompt_example: "the camera pedestals up from the table into a top-down view"

name: Zoom
definition: The camera stays still and only the lens zooms, so the background flattens as it closes in.
when_to_use: Use for a watchful, documentary feel, or a 1970s film look.
prompt_example: "slow zoom in from the wide street to her face in the crowd"

name: Snap Zoom
definition: A split-second zoom from wide to tight.
when_to_use: Use for comedy beats, reactions and punchlines.
prompt_example: "snap zoom onto his face as he realises"

name: Spiral Shot
definition: The camera circles the subject while rising, like a corkscrew.
when_to_use: Use for grand reveals, dream moments and big emotional lifts.
prompt_example: "the camera spirals up around the dancer and rises above the stage"

name: Glide
definition: A slow, weightless drift past the subject, as if carried on a breeze.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy, hypnotic, music-video moods.
prompt_example: "slow weightless glide past her through the flower field"

name: Follow Shot
definition: The camera follows behind someone as they move.
when_to_use: Use to take the viewer on the journey with your character.
prompt_example: "follow shot behind her as she walks into the crowd"

name: FPV Drone
definition: Fast first-person drone flight: the camera is the drone, diving and banking through space.
when_to_use: Use for adrenaline, and for paths no person could ever fly.
prompt_example: "FPV drone dives off the cliff and skims the waves"

name: Camera Roll
definition: The camera rotates around its own lens, tipping the whole picture over.
when_to_use: Use for dizziness, dream logic, or a world turning upside down.
prompt_example: "the camera rolls a full turn as it pushes toward her"

name: Medium Close-Up
definition: From the chest up: closer than a medium shot, looser than a close-up.
when_to_use: Use for conversations that should feel personal without getting in someone's face.
prompt_example: "medium close-up of him leaning in to whisper"

name: Insert Shot
definition: A quick cut to one small detail: a text message, a ring, a button.
when_to_use: Use to hand the viewer one important piece of information fast.
prompt_example: "insert shot of her phone lighting up with a message"

name: Full Shot
definition: The whole person from head to feet, nothing cut off.
when_to_use: Use to show an outfit, a pose, a dance move or a full action.
prompt_example: "full shot of the dancer mid-leap"

name: Eye Level
definition: The camera sits at the subject's eye height, looking straight at them.
when_to_use: Use when you want the angle to feel neutral and honest.
prompt_example: "eye-level shot of her across the kitchen table"

name: Ground Level
definition: The lens sits right on the floor, looking along it.
when_to_use: Use for feet, things rolling past, or a creature's-eye view.
prompt_example: "ground-level shot as the skateboard rolls toward us"

name: Profile Shot
definition: The subject seen exactly side-on.
when_to_use: Use for silhouettes, faces deep in thought, or two people facing off.
prompt_example: "profile shot of him staring out of the train window"

name: Bird's-Eye View
definition: Looking straight down from above.
when_to_use: Use for patterns, maps, choreography, or a calm god's-eye distance.
prompt_example: "bird's-eye view of the dancers forming a circle"

name: Macro Lens
definition: An extreme close lens for tiny details and textures.
when_to_use: Use to make something small feel huge.
prompt_example: "macro shot of a raindrop sliding down a leaf"

name: Atmospheric Haze
definition: Light hangs in the air and the distance fades into soft mist.
when_to_use: Use for depth, mood and visible beams of light.
prompt_example: "atmospheric haze, morning light cutting through the trees"

name: Foreground Wipe
definition: Something passes right in front of the lens and, as it clears, the scene behind has changed.
when_to_use: Use for a smooth one-take feel. One of the easiest transitions to get right in AI video.
prompt_example: "a blurred figure walks across the lens; as they clear frame we are in a new street"

name: Object Portal
definition: A ring, frame or lens held up to the camera shows the next scene inside it, and the camera pushes through.
when_to_use: Use to move into a new place or world in one playful move.
prompt_example: "a ring held up to the lens frames the beach; the camera pushes through it"

name: Hand Over Lens
definition: Hands cover the lens, then open on a new scene.
when_to_use: Use for playful resets and reveals.
prompt_example: "she covers the lens with both hands; as they part she is somewhere new"

name: Push-Through
definition: The camera pushes into something dark and round, like a peephole or a hole, and comes out in the next scene.
when_to_use: Use for curiosity, spy moods and down-the-rabbit-hole jumps.
prompt_example: "the camera pushes into the keyhole and comes out in the next room"

name: Colour Match Cut
definition: The frame fills with one colour, then cuts to something else of the same colour.
when_to_use: Use to link two unrelated scenes in a satisfying way.
prompt_example: "the frame fills with red paint, then cuts to a red umbrella in the rain"

name: Match on Action
definition: An action starts in one shot and finishes in the next.
when_to_use: Use for energy, comedy and cause and effect.
prompt_example: "she throws the ball at the lens and it lands in the next scene"

name: Light Match Cut
definition: A light flares to white, and the next shot opens on a light in the same spot.
when_to_use: Use for time jumps and dreamy montages.
prompt_example: "the lantern flares to white; the next shot is a street lamp in the same place"

name: Morph
definition: One scene smoothly reshapes into another.
when_to_use: Use for signature dream moments. Far easier in AI video than in traditional effects.
prompt_example: "the paper crane slowly reshapes into a white bird"

name: Freeze Frame
definition: The picture freezes on a peak moment, then the next shot starts from that same pose.
when_to_use: Use as a pattern break, a punchline or a 'that's me' moment.
prompt_example: "she leaps; the frame freezes at the top of the jump"

name: Flash to White
definition: The frame blows out to white from a real light, then fades into the next shot.
when_to_use: Use for memories, revelations and impact.
prompt_example: "a camera flash fires and the white fades into the next scene"

name: Fade to Black
definition: The picture fades away to black.
when_to_use: Use for endings, chapter breaks and deliberate pauses. Not between every scene.
prompt_example: "final shot fades to black"

name: Jump Cut
definition: The camera stays put while time jumps between cuts, so things pop in, out or around.
when_to_use: Use for routines, comedy and fast montages.
prompt_example: "jump cuts on a locked frame as more friends appear beside her"

name: Background Swap
definition: The subject stays exactly in place while the world behind them changes.
when_to_use: Use to show time passing or a life changing around one person.
prompt_example: "he stays still while the background cuts from beach to city to snow"

name: Glitch Transition
definition: A burst of digital distortion covers the cut.
when_to_use: Use for tech, gaming and AI topics. Best added in the edit rather than prompted.
prompt_example: "add in the edit: a two-frame RGB glitch between the shots"

name: Light Leak
definition: A warm wash of light sweeps across and covers the cut.
when_to_use: Use for weddings, lifestyle and dreamy beauty edits. Best added in the edit.
prompt_example: "add in the edit: a warm light leak sweeping across the cut"

name: Speed Smear
definition: Something fast whips past the lens and its blur becomes the cut.
when_to_use: Use for racing, sport and anything fast.
prompt_example: "a car zooms past the lens and as the blur clears we are at the finish line"

name: Cel Shading
definition: Flat blocks of color with crisp, hard-edged shadows, like a frame from a hand-painted cartoon. No soft blending, just clean light and dark.
when_to_use: Use when you want a clean animated look for characters, games or scenes. It flattens fine texture, so skip it if you want painterly detail.
prompt_example: "fox courier on a bicycle, cel shading, bright afternoon"

name: Stop Motion
definition: Real little objects moved a tiny bit at a time and photographed frame by frame. Everything has a handmade, slightly jittery charm.
when_to_use: Use for cozy, crafty scenes with puppets, felt or toys. In video, expect a choppy rhythm; that's part of the magic.
prompt_example: "felt mouse baking bread in a tiny kitchen, stop motion"

name: Storybook Illustration
definition: The gentle, detailed pictures you find in a children's picture book. Soft colors, friendly shapes, and a scene that feels like it's mid-story.
when_to_use: Use for warm, wholesome images that feel like a bedtime tale. Add a medium like watercolor or gouache to steer the look.
prompt_example: "badger reading by lantern light in a burrow, storybook illustration"

name: Vector Art
definition: Clean, smooth shapes with sharp edges and flat or simple gradient fills, like a modern app illustration or a logo. No brush texture at all.
when_to_use: Use for icons, stickers, posters and tidy graphics. It can look generic, so give it a strong palette or an unusual subject.
prompt_example: "vector art of a lighthouse at sunset, flat colors, clean shapes"

name: Rubber Hose Animation
definition: The bouncy cartoon style of the 1920s and 30s, where arms and legs bend like noodles with no elbows or knees. Think pie-cut eyes, white gloves and big grins.
when_to_use: Use for cheerful, old-timey characters with lots of bounce. It looks most like itself in black and white or faded color.
prompt_example: "dancing teapot character, rubber hose animation, black and white"

name: Cutout Animation
definition: Characters and scenery made from flat paper pieces, moved around like puppets on a tabletop. You can see the cut edges and the paper grain.
when_to_use: Use for crafty, folk-tale or collage-style stories. Movement looks a little stiff, which is part of the charm.
prompt_example: "paper cutout fox chasing the moon over hills, cutout animation"

name: Rotoscope
definition: Animation traced over real filmed movement, so drawn characters move with lifelike weight and grace. It sits halfway between live action and drawing.
when_to_use: Use when you want drawn characters that move naturally, like a dancer or a runner. In video, expect a slightly wobbly, dreamy line.
prompt_example: "woman dancing in a kitchen, rotoscope animation, bold outlines"

name: Isometric Illustration
definition: A tidy, angled view where everything is seen from above at the same slant, with nothing shrinking into the distance. Like a tiny diorama or a game map.
when_to_use: Use for cute room cutaways, maps and miniature worlds. It doesn't do dramatic perspective, so leave camera angle words out.
prompt_example: "isometric illustration of a cozy bookshop interior, soft colors"

name: Impasto
definition: Paint laid on so thickly that it stands up off the canvas in ridges and peaks. You can almost feel every brushstroke.
when_to_use: Use when you want rich, touchable texture and energy. All that surface can fight with fine detail, so keep the subject simple.
prompt_example: "sunflowers in a clay jug, impasto oil painting"

name: Stippling
definition: Pictures built entirely from tiny dots. Dots packed close together make shadows; spread-out dots make light.
when_to_use: Use for old-book illustrations, botanical studies and ink portraits. It reads best in black and white with one clear subject.
prompt_example: "stippling ink drawing of a barn owl, white paper"

name: Cross-Hatching
definition: Shading made from layers of crisscrossing pen lines. The more lines stack up, the deeper the shadow.
when_to_use: Use for engraved, sketchbook or old-newspaper looks. It can get busy, so pair it with a clear subject.
prompt_example: "cross-hatching pen drawing of an old sailor, dramatic shadows"

name: Sfumato
definition: Soft, smoky blending where edges melt into shadow with no hard lines. A Renaissance painting method that gives faces a hushed, mysterious glow.
when_to_use: Use for gentle, timeless portraits and quiet moods. It softens everything, so it's not the pick for crisp detail.
prompt_example: "portrait of a young scholar, sfumato, warm dim light"

name: Dry Brush
definition: A nearly dry brush dragged across paper or canvas, so the paint skips and leaves scratchy, broken streaks. Rough, airy and full of texture.
when_to_use: Use for wind, grass, weathered wood and rugged landscapes. It's less suited to smooth skin or glossy surfaces.
prompt_example: "wild grass on a windy hill, dry brush painting"

name: Wet-on-Wet
definition: Wet paint dropped onto paper that is already wet, so colors bloom, bleed and feather into each other. Soft, unpredictable and lovely.
when_to_use: Use for skies, misty backgrounds, flowers and dreamy moods. You give up control, so don't expect sharp lines.
prompt_example: "wet-on-wet watercolor of a stormy sea sky"

name: Palette Knife
definition: Paint spread with a flat metal knife instead of a brush, leaving smooth, chunky slabs of color with sharp edges. Bold and almost sculpted.
when_to_use: Use for bright landscapes, city lights and flowers with lots of energy. Fine detail gets lost, so think in big shapes.
prompt_example: "rainy city street at night, palette knife painting"

name: Gold Leaf
definition: Paper-thin sheets of real gold pressed onto a surface, so parts of the art shine like metal. You see it in old religious icons, illuminated manuscripts and lacquerware.
when_to_use: Use for a precious, glowing accent on halos, borders or backgrounds. A little goes a long way; too much looks flat and brassy.
prompt_example: "heron among reeds, ink painting with gold leaf background"

name: Madhubani Painting
definition: A folk painting tradition from the Mithila region of Bihar, India, and nearby Nepal. Bold double outlines filled with bright color and pattern, showing fish, peacocks, gods and trees of life.
when_to_use: Use for joyful, densely patterned scenes from nature or myth. Name it directly; a vague 'Indian art' gives a muddier result.
prompt_example: "Madhubani painting of two peacocks under a tree, bright colors"

name: Persian Miniature
definition: Small, richly detailed paintings made for illustrated books in Persia, today's Iran. Flat, layered spaces, jewel colors, patterned carpets and gardens, often edged in gold.
when_to_use: Use for storytelling scenes full of tiny figures, palaces and gardens. It doesn't do deep, realistic perspective, and that's part of its beauty.
prompt_example: "Persian miniature of a garden gathering with musicians, gold border"

name: Papel Picado
definition: Mexican tissue paper banners with delicate cut-out flowers, birds and skulls, strung in bright rows overhead.
when_to_use: Use for festive streets, celebrations and Dia de los Muertos scenes. It is part of real family traditions, so keep the setting joyful and respectful.
prompt_example: "village plaza strung with papel picado banners, warm evening light"

name: Azulejo Tiles
definition: Painted, glazed ceramic tiles that cover walls, churches and whole building fronts in Portugal. Best known in cobalt blue on white, with swirling flowers and painted scenes.
when_to_use: Use for sunny architecture, kitchens, patterns and travel scenes. Say 'blue and white' for the classic look, since azulejos come in many colors.
prompt_example: "Lisbon doorway covered in azulejo tiles, morning light"

name: Batik
definition: Cloth decorated with a wax-resist method: wax blocks the dye in some places, leaving the pattern behind. Famous in Indonesia, especially Java, often with fine crackle lines where the wax broke.
when_to_use: Use for flowing textile patterns, fabric backgrounds and clothing. Mention colors and motifs, like flowers, birds or waves, to guide it.
prompt_example: "batik fabric with birds and vines, indigo and brown"

name: Chinese Ink Wash Painting
definition: Black ink brushed onto paper or silk, from deep strokes to pale grey washes. Misty mountains, bamboo, and lots of quiet empty space.
when_to_use: Use for calm, poetic landscapes and nature studies. It's mostly black and grey, so add 'light color' if you want a touch of tint.
prompt_example: "Chinese ink wash painting of mountains in mist, a small boat"

name: Islamic Geometric Pattern
definition: Interlocking stars, polygons and rosettes that repeat endlessly, found in tilework, carved wood and plaster across the Islamic world. Precise, balanced and mesmerizing.
when_to_use: Use for tiles, ceilings, doorways and decorative backgrounds. AI can get the geometry slightly off, so expect to pick the cleanest result.
prompt_example: "courtyard ceiling with Islamic geometric pattern, turquoise and gold tiles"

name: Tenango Embroidery
definition: Hand-stitched designs from Otomi (Hñähñu) communities around Tenango de Doria in Hidalgo, Mexico. Playful animals, birds and plants in bright thread on white cotton, sometimes all in one color.
when_to_use: Use for joyful textile art, pillows, clothing and pattern backgrounds. Name the tradition instead of a vague 'Mexican pattern' to get the real look.
prompt_example: "Tenango embroidery of deer and flowers, rainbow thread on white cloth"

name: Chibi
definition: A tiny, super-cute character style with a big head, a small body and stubby limbs. Usually only two or three heads tall.
when_to_use: Use for stickers, mascots and funny reaction art. It's not built for drama or realistic proportions.
prompt_example: "chibi knight hugging a giant strawberry, pastel colors"

name: Shoujo Style
definition: The romantic look of manga made mainly for girls and young women. Huge sparkling eyes, flowing hair, and flowers or sparkles floating behind the characters.
when_to_use: Use for tender, emotional and romantic moments. Add 'retro' if you want the older, softer look with lots of dotted shading.
prompt_example: "shoujo style portrait, girl in the rain, roses and sparkles"

name: Shonen Style
definition: The bold, high-energy look of action manga made mainly for boys and teens. Spiky hair, determined faces, sharp angles and big dynamic poses.
when_to_use: Use for battles, sports and hero moments full of movement. It can feel loud, so it's less suited to quiet scenes.
prompt_example: "shonen style hero leaping across rooftops, speed lines, sunset"

name: Mecha
definition: Giant piloted robots, a big part of anime for decades. Think towering armored machines with glowing visors, panel lines and thrusters.
when_to_use: Use for sci-fi scale and heroic machinery. Hands and joints can come out messy, so wide shots often look best.
prompt_example: "white mecha kneeling in a rainy hangar, glowing visor"

name: Speed Lines
definition: Sharp streaks bursting out from or racing behind a subject to show speed, impact or shock. Classic manga shorthand for 'something big just happened.'
when_to_use: Use for action, surprise and comedy beats. It's a drawn effect, so it fits illustrated styles better than photos.
prompt_example: "manga panel of a cat sprinting, speed lines, black and white"

name: Screentone
definition: The dotty grey shading in black and white manga, made from patterns of tiny printed dots. It adds shadow and tone without any color.
when_to_use: Use when you want the feel of a real printed manga page. It only makes sense in black and white or very limited color.
prompt_example: "manga page, girl on a train at dusk, screentone shading"

name: 90s Anime
definition: The hand-painted look of anime from the 1990s: soft film grain, slightly faded colors, sharp-cornered hair and moody city nights.
when_to_use: Use for nostalgic, cinematic anime scenes. Add 'cel animation' to push it further away from glossy modern anime.
prompt_example: "90s anime still, girl on a rooftop at night, city lights"

name: Magical Girl
definition: A beloved anime genre where everyday girls transform into sparkling heroines. Ribbons, wands, frills, starry light and twirling transformation poses.
when_to_use: Use for bright, hopeful heroines and transformation moments. It leans sweet and sparkly, so it's not the pick for gritty fantasy.
prompt_example: "magical girl transformation, ribbons of light, starry pink sky"

name: -core
definition: Add -core to almost any word and it becomes a whole mood: cottagecore, goblincore, normcore. It tells the AI to build a world of objects, colors and clothing around that one idea.
when_to_use: Use to turn a single theme into a full aesthetic. Brand-new combos may be too new for the AI to know, so add a few details too.
prompt_example: "mushroomcore reading nook, moss, soft window light"

name: -punk
definition: From cyberpunk and steampunk, -punk means 'imagine a whole world powered by this.' Solarpunk runs on sunlight and gardens; steampunk runs on brass and steam.
when_to_use: Use to invent a world with its own technology and attitude. Pair it with a material or era so the AI knows what the world is built from.
prompt_example: "solarpunk village with rooftop gardens, bright morning"

name: -wave
definition: Borrowed from music names like vaporwave and synthwave, -wave suggests a retro, nostalgic mood with a strong color palette. Often glowy, dreamy and a little surreal.
when_to_use: Use when you want an image to feel like a remembered era or a soundtrack. Results lean pink, purple and neon, so name other colors if you want them.
prompt_example: "synthwave desert highway, glowing sunset, grid horizon"

name: -kei
definition: Kei is Japanese for 'style' or 'type,' used in street fashion names like mori kei and dolly kei. Adding it suggests a full Japanese street-style outfit built around one idea.
when_to_use: Use for fashion portraits and character outfits. It's about clothing and styling, so it does little for landscapes.
prompt_example: "teatime kei outfit, lace and pastel layers, street portrait"

name: -academia
definition: From dark academia and light academia, -academia wraps a theme in old libraries, tweed, candlelit study and handwritten notes.
when_to_use: Use for bookish scenes and outfits with a twist. Swap the first word to change the mood, like ocean academia or space academia.
prompt_example: "ocean academia study, seashells on old books, rainy window"

name: -gaze
definition: Taken from shoegaze, a hazy, dreamy style of rock music. Adding -gaze suggests soft blur, washed-out color and a floaty, half-remembered feeling.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy, out-of-focus moods and album-cover style art. It blurs things on purpose, so it's not for crisp detail.
prompt_example: "dreamgaze field at dusk, soft blur, faded pink light"

name: -goth
definition: Add -goth to a word to give it a dark, romantic twist: pastel goth, whimsigoth, bubble goth. Black lace, moons and moody shadows, mixed with whatever comes in front.
when_to_use: Use to make a sweet or ordinary theme a little spooky and dramatic. The word in front sets the mood, so choose it with care.
prompt_example: "garden goth tea party, black roses, overcast light"

name: -luxe
definition: From 'deluxe,' -luxe adds a polished, expensive feeling to any theme: boho luxe, night luxe, coastal luxe. Think rich fabrics, soft gold and careful styling.
when_to_use: Use for interiors, fashion and product shots that should feel high-end. On its own it can look generic, so give it a clear theme in front.
prompt_example: "desert luxe bedroom, linen, brass lamp, golden hour"

name: Dust Particles
definition: Tiny specks floating in the air, glowing where a beam of light catches them. They make a room feel still, old and lived-in.
when_to_use: Use in sunny windows, attics, libraries and quiet moments. They only show up well when there's a strong beam of light to catch them.
prompt_example: "old library in the morning, dust particles in a sunbeam"

name: Floating Embers
definition: Glowing orange sparks drifting up from a fire into the dark. Warm, a little dangerous, and a little magical.
when_to_use: Use for campfires, forges, battles and moody fantasy. They need darkness around them, so they fade away in bright daylight.
prompt_example: "blacksmith at the forge, floating embers, dark workshop"

name: Holographic Shimmer
definition: A rainbow sheen that shifts across a surface, like a hologram sticker or a soap bubble. Colors slide from pink to blue to gold as the light moves.
when_to_use: Use for futuristic fashion, packaging, stickers and dreamy objects. It's a bit loud, so put it on one thing rather than the whole scene.
prompt_example: "holographic shimmer jacket, white studio, soft light"

name: Light Trails
definition: Smooth ribbons of light left behind by moving cars, sparklers or dancers. It looks like the light is drawing lines through the air.
when_to_use: Use for night streets, celebrations and movement. In still images it reads like a long-exposure photo; in video, expect streaks that follow motion.
prompt_example: "city bridge at night, red and white light trails"

name: Chromatic Aberration
definition: Thin red and blue color fringes along the edges of things, like an old or cheap lens splitting the light. It gives a slightly glitchy, retro camera feel.
when_to_use: Use for edgy, retro, dreamlike or sci-fi looks. A little goes far; too much just looks blurry.
prompt_example: "skateboarder at dusk, chromatic aberration, grainy film"

name: Double Exposure
definition: Two pictures blended into one, like a person's silhouette filled with a forest or a city. Dreamy and poetic, as if memories overlap.
when_to_use: Use for album covers, posters and emotional portraits. Keep both images simple, or the blend turns to mush.
prompt_example: "double exposure of a woman's profile and a pine forest"

name: Ink in Water
definition: Clouds of ink blooming and curling slowly through clear water. Soft, swirling shapes that feel alive.
when_to_use: Use for abstract backgrounds, title cards and calm, hypnotic video. It's a mood rather than a subject, so add color words.
prompt_example: "purple and gold ink in water, slow swirl, black background"

name: Shattering Glass
definition: Glass breaking into a burst of sharp, glittering shards, either frozen in midair or flying outward. Instant drama.
when_to_use: Use for action, product shots and big surprise moments. Hands and faces close to the shards can come out messy, so give them space.
prompt_example: "perfume bottle shattering, glass shards frozen midair, black background"

name: Freckles
definition: Small, scattered brown spots across the nose, cheeks and shoulders. They add warmth and personality to a face.
when_to_use: Use to make portraits feel natural and less airbrushed. Say 'light freckles' if they come out too heavy.
prompt_example: "portrait of a smiling teenager with freckles, soft window light"

name: Silver Hair
definition: Shining grey-white hair with a soft metallic glow in the light. It reads as graceful age, or as a bold fashion color on anyone.
when_to_use: Use for older characters with dignity, or for striking fashion portraits. Add an age word if you want the AI to read it one way.
prompt_example: "woman in her seventies with silver hair, linen shirt, garden"

name: Laugh Lines
definition: The soft creases around the eyes and mouth that come from years of smiling. They make a face look kind and lived-in.
when_to_use: Use for honest, warm portraits of adults, especially older people. AI tends to smooth skin, so this word helps keep real character.
prompt_example: "close-up of a fisherman with laugh lines, overcast light"

name: Gentle Smile
definition: A soft, closed-lip or barely open smile. Calm and kind, rather than a big toothy grin.
when_to_use: Use when a big grin feels fake or too much. Lovely for portraits, book covers and quiet moments.
prompt_example: "older man with a gentle smile, holding a teacup, warm light"

name: Relaxed Posture
definition: Loose shoulders, an easy stance and a body at rest, like someone leaning on a wall or settled into a chair. The opposite of stiff and posed.
when_to_use: Use to make people look comfortable and natural instead of mannequin-like. Add the action, like leaning or sitting, for the best results.
prompt_example: "young man in a relaxed posture leaning on a cafe counter, morning light"

name: Box Braids
definition: Long braids sectioned into neat squares at the scalp, a protective style with deep roots in African and Black hair traditions. Worn down, up, or gathered into a high bun.
when_to_use: Use for accurate, respectful portraits and characters with braided hair. Add length or details, like 'waist-length' or 'with gold cuffs.'
prompt_example: "portrait of a woman with long box braids, gold hair cuffs, studio light"

name: Messy Bun
definition: Hair twisted up loosely on top of the head, with soft strands falling free. Casual, busy and comfortable.
when_to_use: Use for cozy, everyday, at-home or working scenes. It reads as informal, so skip it for formal portraits.
prompt_example: "artist with a messy bun painting at an easel, afternoon light"

name: Middle-Aged
definition: Roughly between 40 and 60, with gentle signs of age like a few grey hairs and soft lines. A simple way to stop the AI from making everyone look 25.
when_to_use: Use whenever age matters to the story. For more precision, give a decade, like 'in her fifties.'
prompt_example: "middle-aged teacher grading papers at a kitchen table, lamplight"

name: Mad Scientist
definition: A wild-haired genius in a lab coat, surrounded by bubbling flasks, sparks and strange machines. Brilliant, a bit unhinged, and always mid-experiment.
when_to_use: Use for spooky, funny or sci-fi scenes full of fun props. It leans cartoonish, so add 'realistic' if you want it grounded.
prompt_example: "mad scientist in a stone lab, glowing green flasks, lightning outside"

name: Femme Fatale
definition: The glamorous, mysterious woman of old crime films, calm and clever, whose charm hides danger. Think sharp tailoring, window-blind shadows and a knowing look.
when_to_use: Use for noir scenes and moody, stylish character portraits. It's a well-worn type, so give her a goal or a job to make her more than a cliche.
prompt_example: "femme fatale in a trench coat, rainy street, noir lighting"

name: Grizzled Detective
definition: A tired, weather-beaten investigator with stubble, a rumpled coat and a long memory. They've seen too much and keep going anyway.
when_to_use: Use for crime stories, rainy cities and late-night offices. Add a city and an era to keep it from looking like every other noir.
prompt_example: "grizzled detective under a streetlamp, rain, neon reflections"

name: Wise Mentor
definition: The calm, older guide who teaches the hero, often with a walking staff, a long beard or a cup of tea. Patient, knowing and a little mysterious.
when_to_use: Use for fantasy, training and coming-of-age scenes. Try unexpected ages, settings or styles so it doesn't feel stale.
prompt_example: "wise mentor teaching a young apprentice by a mountain fire"

name: Lovable Rogue
definition: A charming scoundrel with a crooked grin, quick hands and a heart of gold underneath. Rules are more like suggestions.
when_to_use: Use for adventure, heist and swashbuckling scenes. Show them mid-mischief, like picking a lock or dodging a guard, for more personality.
prompt_example: "lovable rogue grinning on a ship's rigging, golden hour"

name: Gentle Giant
definition: A huge, strong character who turns out to be soft-hearted and kind. Big hands, careful movements, and often a tiny friend nearby.
when_to_use: Use for heartwarming scenes that play big against small. It works for people, creatures and animals alike.
prompt_example: "gentle giant troll holding a baby bird, misty forest"

name: Absent-Minded Professor
definition: A brilliant, scattered thinker lost in their own ideas, with glasses pushed up, chalk on one sleeve and papers everywhere.
when_to_use: Use for cozy, comic or academic scenes full of clutter. Pairs nicely with an -academia mood for a bookish look.
prompt_example: "absent-minded professor in a cluttered study, chalkboard full of equations"

name: Plucky Sidekick
definition: The small, brave, loyal friend who follows the hero everywhere, ready with a joke or a rescue. Full of heart and a little bit clumsy.
when_to_use: Use for adventure and comedy scenes that need energy and warmth. Show them beside the hero so the role reads clearly.
prompt_example: "plucky sidekick fox riding on a knight's shoulder, sunny meadow"

name: Octane Render
definition: A glossy, ultra-clean 3D look with crisp reflections and soft, believable light. Everything looks freshly made and expensive.
when_to_use: Use when you want polished 3D art, toys or products that shine. It can feel a bit too perfect, so add texture words if you want warmth.
prompt_example: "glass perfume bottle on wet black stone, octane render"

name: Clay Render
definition: Everything is shown in plain, smooth, matte clay, usually one soft gray or white. Shapes and shadows do all the talking.
when_to_use: Use to show off form and lighting without color getting in the way. Not the pick if you need color or fine surface detail.
prompt_example: "teapot on a windowsill, clay render, soft studio light"

name: Wireframe Render
definition: The 3D object is drawn as a see-through mesh of thin glowing lines, like the skeleton of a computer model.
when_to_use: Use for tech, sci-fi and blueprint moods. It reads best on a dark background, and busy scenes can turn into a tangle of lines.
prompt_example: "sports car wireframe render, cyan lines on black"

name: Isometric Render
definition: A tidy 3D view from above at an angle, with no vanishing point, so it looks like a little game board or dollhouse.
when_to_use: Use for cozy rooms, tiny towns and explainer art. The camera angle is fixed, so it is not for dramatic or cinematic shots.
prompt_example: "isometric render of a tiny bakery, warm morning light"

name: Cel-Shaded Render
definition: 3D shapes painted with flat blocks of color and bold outlines, so they look like a cartoon or anime drawing.
when_to_use: Use when you want 3D depth with a hand-drawn feel, great for characters and game scenes. Fine painterly detail gets flattened.
prompt_example: "fox adventurer on a cliff, cel-shaded render, bright sky"

name: Ray Tracing
definition: A 3D look where light bounces like it does in real life, giving true reflections in puddles, glass and shiny floors.
when_to_use: Use when reflections matter, like rainy streets, mirrors or chrome. It is a hint toward realism, not a magic fix for a weak prompt.
prompt_example: "rainy neon alley at night, ray tracing, reflections in puddles"

name: Subsurface Scattering
definition: The soft glow you see when light sinks into something and lights it from inside, like a backlit ear, a grape or a wax candle.
when_to_use: Use to make skin, fruit, jade or wax feel alive instead of plastic. It is subtle, so pair it with backlight to really see it.
prompt_example: "jade dragon figurine, subsurface scattering, backlit"

name: Product Render
definition: A spotless studio shot of an object made in 3D, floating or sitting on a simple backdrop with clean, flattering light.
when_to_use: Use for packaging ideas, gadgets and mockups. Real logos and tiny printed text often come out garbled, so keep labels simple.
prompt_example: "wireless earbuds on a pastel pedestal, product render"

name: Houndstooth
definition: A broken check made of little jagged four-pointed shapes, usually black and white. Classic, sharp and a little bit British tailoring.
when_to_use: Use for fashion, coats and smart retro looks. Large areas of it can shimmer or warp, so keep it on clothing or trim.
prompt_example: "woman in a houndstooth coat on a rainy street"

name: Paisley
definition: Curving teardrop shapes packed with tiny swirls and flowers. The motif came from Persia and India, and was named after the Scottish town that wove it into shawls.
when_to_use: Use for rich textiles, bandanas, wallpaper and boho fashion. It gets busy fast, so give it room or limit the colors.
prompt_example: "silk scarf with red and gold paisley, flat lay"

name: Chevron
definition: Bold zigzag stripes stacked into rows of V shapes. Energetic and graphic, like a lightning bolt on repeat.
when_to_use: Use for rugs, wallpaper, sportswear and playful backgrounds. Simple and strong, but it can look dated if the colors are loud.
prompt_example: "living room with a mustard and white chevron rug"

name: Ikat
definition: A woven pattern with soft, feathery edges, because the threads are dyed in sections before weaving. It is a centuries-old craft from places like Indonesia, Central Asia and India.
when_to_use: Use for warm, handmade textiles with a blurred, dreamy edge. AI often makes it too sharp, so ask for blurred edges and woven texture.
prompt_example: "indigo ikat cushion on a rattan chair, blurred feathered edges"

name: Herringbone
definition: Rows of short slanted lines that flip direction, like the bones of a fish. Found in tweed fabric and parquet wood floors.
when_to_use: Use for cozy tailoring, wooden floors and tiled walls. From far away it can look like plain texture, so get closer if you want it seen.
prompt_example: "herringbone oak floor in a sunny reading nook"

name: Gingham
definition: An even checkered pattern made by crossing stripes of one color with white. Think picnic blankets and summer dresses.
when_to_use: Use for sweet, homey, countryside feels. It reads as cute and simple, so it is not the choice for edgy or luxury moods.
prompt_example: "picnic basket on a red gingham blanket, summer meadow"

name: Argyle
definition: Rows of diamonds with thin diagonal lines crossing over them. Named after Argyll in Scotland, where a clan tartan inspired it, and famous on knit socks and sweaters.
when_to_use: Use for preppy knits, golf clothes and cozy academic looks. It works best on knitwear, flat surfaces can look like a game board.
prompt_example: "cozy argyle sweater, autumn library, warm light"

name: Seigaiha
definition: Overlapping half circles stacked like fish scales, each one a little wave. A traditional Japanese pattern meaning calm seas and good luck.
when_to_use: Use for kimonos, wrapping paper, tiles and calm ocean themes. Ask for gold or indigo lines to keep it looking refined.
prompt_example: "seigaiha wave pattern, gold lines on deep indigo"

name: Miniature
definition: Everything looks tiny and handmade, like a scale model or a toy town you could hold in your hands.
when_to_use: Use to make big scenes feel cute and collectible. Real people can end up looking like little figurines, which is part of the charm.
prompt_example: "miniature Paris cafe on a fingertip, macro photography"

name: Diorama
definition: A little 3D scene built inside a box or on a base, with a painted backdrop and tiny props, like a museum display.
when_to_use: Use to frame a whole world in one neat little stage. It works best with one clear setting rather than many things at once.
prompt_example: "diorama of a rainy forest cabin inside a wooden box"

name: Knolling
definition: Objects laid out flat and lined up at neat right angles, every item in its own space. Very tidy and very satisfying.
when_to_use: Use for tool kits, gear layouts and 'what's in my bag' images. AI can repeat or merge items, so keep the object list short.
prompt_example: "knolling of vintage camera gear on kraft paper, top-down"

name: Flat Lay
definition: A photo taken straight down at things arranged on a table or floor. Casual, styled and very social media.
when_to_use: Use for food, fashion outfits, stationery and product moods. Unlike knolling, it can be loose and artful rather than strictly lined up.
prompt_example: "flat lay of a cozy breakfast, linen napkin, morning light"

name: Cutaway
definition: A view with part of the outside removed so you can see inside, like a house with the front wall missing.
when_to_use: Use to show rooms, machines or creatures inside a shell. It can get messy with too many rooms, so name the ones you want.
prompt_example: "cutaway of a cozy treehouse showing every room"

name: Exploded View
definition: An object pulled apart into its pieces, all floating in order, so you can see how it fits together.
when_to_use: Use for gadgets, sneakers, burgers and anything fun to take apart. The parts may not be accurate, so treat it as art, not instructions.
prompt_example: "exploded view of a cheeseburger, studio light, white background"

name: Character Sheet
definition: One character shown several times on a single page, usually front, side and back, sometimes with faces and outfits too.
when_to_use: Use when you want to design a character and keep them consistent later. Small details can change between poses, so check each one.
prompt_example: "character sheet of a young witch, front side and back views"

name: Sticker Sheet
definition: A page of little die-cut stickers with white borders, each one a cute, simple picture on its own.
when_to_use: Use for cute sets of icons, animals or doodles in one image. Text on stickers often comes out jumbled, so stick to pictures.
prompt_example: "sticker sheet of happy vegetables, white borders, pastel colors"

name: Cobalt Blue
definition: A strong, bright, pure blue, deeper than sky blue and brighter than navy. Think of blue glass bottles and painted pottery.
when_to_use: Use when you want a bold blue that feels clean and confident. It can overpower a scene, so use it for one star element.
prompt_example: "cobalt blue door on a whitewashed wall, bright sun"

name: Sage Green
definition: A soft, gray-green, like the leaves of the sage plant. Calm, earthy and easy on the eyes.
when_to_use: Use for calm interiors, wedding themes and natural, gentle looks. It is quiet on purpose, so it will not grab attention.
prompt_example: "sage green kitchen with brass handles, morning light"

name: Terracotta
definition: A warm, earthy orange-brown, the color of baked clay pots and roof tiles.
when_to_use: Use for sunny, rustic and Mediterranean-feeling scenes. It pairs beautifully with blues and greens, but can feel heavy with only browns.
prompt_example: "terracotta pots on a sunny balcony, olive trees"

name: Mustard Yellow
definition: A warm, slightly brown yellow, softer than lemon and richer than butter. Very vintage, very cozy.
when_to_use: Use for retro fashion, 70s rooms and warm autumn feels. It can look muddy next to gray, so pair it with blue, teal or burgundy.
prompt_example: "mustard yellow armchair in a retro living room"

name: Burgundy
definition: A deep, rich red with a hint of purple, like red wine in a glass.
when_to_use: Use for elegant, romantic and moody scenes, from velvet chairs to winter fashion. In dark scenes it can read as black, so give it light.
prompt_example: "burgundy velvet gown in a candlelit hall"

name: Dusty Rose
definition: A muted, grayish pink, softer and calmer than bubblegum. Like old roses or faded silk.
when_to_use: Use for gentle, romantic and vintage looks. If you want pink that pops, choose a brighter pink instead.
prompt_example: "dusty rose bridesmaid dresses in a garden"

name: Coral
definition: A lively pinkish orange, warm and happy, like a summer sunset or tropical flowers.
when_to_use: Use for cheerful, beachy and summery images. It can look loud next to other bright colors, so pair it with white, navy or teal.
prompt_example: "coral beach hut against a turquoise sea"

name: Lavender
definition: A pale, soft purple, like the flowers of the lavender plant. Gentle, dreamy and a little bit magical.
when_to_use: Use for calm, sweet and fairy tale moods. It can wash out in bright light, so add a deeper purple if the image feels faded.
prompt_example: "lavender field at dusk, soft haze"

name: Vantablack
definition: One of the darkest materials ever made, a black so deep it swallows almost all light. Objects coated in it look like flat holes cut out of the world.
when_to_use: Use for eerie, mind-bending objects and dramatic contrast. AI can only fake it, so expect a very deep black rather than true lightlessness.
prompt_example: "vantablack sphere on a white marble floor, gallery light"
tags: dark colors;black and white;weird and wonderful;spooky

name: YInMn Blue
definition: A vivid, electric blue pigment discovered by accident in a university lab in 2009. Named after the elements in it: yttrium, indium and manganese.
when_to_use: Use when you want a blue that feels brighter and more modern than royal blue. The AI may not know it well, so add 'vivid electric blue' too.
prompt_example: "ceramic vase glazed in YInMn blue, vivid electric blue, white studio"

name: Prussian Blue
definition: A deep, inky blue with a touch of green, made in Berlin around 1706. It is the blue of old blueprints and famous Japanese wave prints.
when_to_use: Use for rich night skies, ink art and moody seas. It can feel almost black in small images, so give it some light.
prompt_example: "stormy sea in prussian blue ink, woodblock print style"

name: Duochrome
definition: A finish that shifts between two colors as you move, like a beetle shell or shimmery eyeshadow going from purple to green.
when_to_use: Use for cars, makeup, beetles and futuristic fashion. It is related to iridescent, but duochrome sticks to just two colors.
prompt_example: "duochrome sports car, purple to green color shift, studio"

name: Chartreuse
definition: A sharp yellow-green, halfway between lime and lemon, named after a French herbal liqueur. Bold, zesty and a little bit odd.
when_to_use: Use when you want a fresh, eye-grabbing color that feels fashion-forward. Too much can look sickly, so use it as an accent.
prompt_example: "model in a chartreuse coat against a lilac wall"

name: Tyrian Purple
definition: An ancient reddish purple dye made from sea snails. It was so costly to make that it became the color of emperors and kings.
when_to_use: Use for royal robes, rich fabrics and ancient feeling scenes. The AI may just give a regular purple, so add 'deep reddish purple'.
prompt_example: "queen in tyrian purple robes, torchlit marble hall"

name: Verdigris
definition: The chalky blue-green crust that grows on old copper, brass and bronze, like on old statues and church roofs.
when_to_use: Use for aged metal, fantasy ruins and steampunk details. It is a texture as much as a color, so it shines on metal surfaces.
prompt_example: "verdigris copper dome above a foggy old city"

name: Ultramarine
definition: A deep, glowing blue first made by grinding the stone lapis lazuli. In the Renaissance it could cost more than gold.
when_to_use: Use for heavenly skies, sacred art and rich blue robes. It leans slightly purple, so ask for cobalt blue if you want a cleaner blue.
prompt_example: "angel in ultramarine robes, gold leaf halo, fresco"

name: Watercolor Over Photograph
definition: A real photo with loose watercolor washes painted on top, so parts of the picture melt into soft, colorful paint.
when_to_use: Use to make a photo feel like a memory or a travel journal page. Faces can get blurred, so say where the paint should go.
prompt_example: "street photo of Venice, watercolor over photograph, paint bleeding at the edges"

name: Embroidered Photo
definition: A printed photo with real-looking stitches sewn right into it, adding thread flowers, halos or colored patterns.
when_to_use: Use for handmade, nostalgic and quirky portraits. Stitch detail works best when large and simple, tiny stitches can smudge.
prompt_example: "vintage portrait with embroidered flower crown, colorful thread"

name: Paper and Neon
definition: Soft cut-paper shapes lit up by glowing neon tubes, so the cozy and the electric sit side by side.
when_to_use: Use for night scenes, signs and dreamy city art with a handmade touch. It works best in dark settings where the glow can show.
prompt_example: "cut paper city skyline with pink neon outlines, night"

name: Doodles on Photo
definition: A real photo with playful white or colored doodles drawn over it, like hearts, wings, sparkles and little faces.
when_to_use: Use for fun social posts, cheeky portraits and pet photos. Keep the doodles simple, busy drawings can bury the photo.
prompt_example: "photo of a corgi with white doodle wings and a crown"

name: Charcoal and Gold Leaf
definition: Smudgy black charcoal drawing with shining patches of real-looking gold leaf. Moody and precious at once.
when_to_use: Use for elegant portraits, animals and sacred-feeling art. Gold can look flat yellow, so ask for 'metallic gold leaf' to keep the shine.
prompt_example: "charcoal sketch of a horse with metallic gold leaf mane"

name: Collage and Paint
definition: Torn paper, old photos and magazine bits glued down, then painted over with bold brushstrokes.
when_to_use: Use for artsy, layered and expressive images with a scrapbook feel. It is busy by nature, so keep one clear subject.
prompt_example: "collage and paint portrait, torn maps, bold red brushstrokes"

name: Ink and Watercolor
definition: Crisp pen lines with soft watercolor washes under them. The lines hold the shape, the paint adds mood.
when_to_use: Use when plain watercolor gets too blurry and you want clear detail. Great for travel sketches, botanicals and storybook scenes.
prompt_example: "ink and watercolor sketch of a corner cafe in the rain"

name: Pressed Flowers and Ink
definition: Real flattened flowers and leaves combined with ink drawing, so petals become a dress, hair or wings on a sketched figure.
when_to_use: Use for gentle, nature-filled art and botanical portraits. It works best on plain paper backgrounds, which keep it clean.
prompt_example: "ink sketch of a dancer with a skirt of pressed flowers"

name: Solarpunk
definition: A bright, hopeful future where cities are covered in gardens, solar panels and clean energy. Nature and technology get along.
when_to_use: Use for optimistic sci-fi and green city dreams. If it looks too plain, add details like rooftop farms, vines and stained glass.
prompt_example: "solarpunk city with rooftop gardens and white towers, sunny day"

name: Dieselpunk
definition: A gritty, alternate past powered by oil and engines, inspired by the 1920s to 1940s. Think riveted airships, smoke and heavy machines.
when_to_use: Use for moody adventure and alternate history scenes. It is darker and heavier than steampunk, with less brass and more steel.
prompt_example: "dieselpunk airship over a smoky industrial city, dusk"

name: Underwater City
definition: A whole town under the sea, with glass domes, glowing windows and fish drifting past the streets.
