when_to_use: Use for dreamy fantasy and sci-fi worlds. Add light words like light rays or bioluminescence, or it can look murky.
prompt_example: "underwater city of glass domes, light rays, schools of fish"

name: Sky Islands
definition: Floating chunks of land drifting in the clouds, with waterfalls spilling off their edges into the sky.
when_to_use: Use for epic fantasy views and dreamy adventure scenes. It looks best wide, so pair it with a wide shot.
prompt_example: "sky islands with waterfalls, tiny village, golden clouds"

name: Steampunk
definition: A Victorian-style world run on steam, with brass gears, goggles, clockwork gadgets and airships.
when_to_use: Use for inventors, fantasy machines and old-world adventure. It is very popular, so add your own twist to stand out.
prompt_example: "steampunk inventor in a workshop full of brass gears"

name: Lunarpunk
definition: The nighttime sister of solarpunk, a peaceful, nature-loving future lit by moonlight, glowing plants and soft lanterns.
when_to_use: Use for mystical, calm and magical night worlds. It is a newer word, so describe the glow and moonlight too.
prompt_example: "lunarpunk village, glowing mushrooms, moonlit river"

name: Overgrown Ruins
definition: Old buildings swallowed by nature, with vines, trees and moss growing through broken walls and windows.
when_to_use: Use for peaceful after-the-end worlds, lost temples and quiet adventure. Add light like golden hour or fog to set the feeling.
prompt_example: "overgrown ruins of a train station, vines, soft sunbeams"

name: Crystal Caverns
definition: Huge caves filled with giant glowing crystals in every color, sparkling like the inside of a geode.
when_to_use: Use for fantasy quests, magical hideaways and jewel-like scenes. Name a color or two, or it can turn into a rainbow mess.
prompt_example: "explorer in crystal caverns, giant purple crystals, soft glow"

name: Impossible Staircase
definition: Stairs that seem to climb forever in a loop, always going up yet ending where they started.
when_to_use: Use for puzzling, dreamlike architecture. AI often makes ordinary stairs, so add 'endless looping stairs' and a high angle.
prompt_example: "impossible staircase looping around a stone tower, high angle"

name: Forced Perspective
definition: A trick where something near the camera lines up with something far away, so a person seems to pinch the moon or hold up a tower.
when_to_use: Use for playful travel shots and giant or tiny effects. It needs a clear near subject and far subject, so describe both.
prompt_example: "forced perspective, girl pinching the full moon between her fingers"

name: Trompe l'Oeil
definition: French for 'fools the eye'. A flat painting so realistic it looks like real windows, doors or objects popping out of the wall.
when_to_use: Use for murals, painted ceilings and walls that seem to open up. It shines most when you show the flat wall around the painting.
prompt_example: "trompe l'oeil mural of an open window to the sea on a brick wall"

name: Hidden Image
definition: A picture with a second picture tucked inside it, like a forest whose trees form a face when you step back.
when_to_use: Use for puzzles, posters and magical double meanings. It is tricky for AI, so name both images clearly and keep the scene simple.
prompt_example: "autumn forest where the trees form a hidden image of an owl"

name: Impossible Triangle
definition: A solid-looking triangle whose three beams join in a way that could never exist in real space.
when_to_use: Use for logos, sculptures and puzzling architecture. AI often fixes it into a normal triangle, so add 'optical illusion' to the prompt.
prompt_example: "impossible triangle sculpture in a desert, optical illusion"

name: Figure-Ground Illusion
definition: A picture you can read two ways, like a white vase that is also two dark faces looking at each other.
when_to_use: Use for clever posters, logos and dreamy portraits. It works best with two flat colors and simple shapes.
prompt_example: "figure-ground illusion, two faces forming a vase, black and white"

name: Infinity Mirror
definition: Two mirrors facing each other, making lights or reflections repeat in a tunnel that seems to go on forever.
when_to_use: Use for glowing art rooms, dreamy portraits and sci-fi halls. It loves points of light, so add lanterns, LEDs or neon.
prompt_example: "infinity mirror room filled with tiny pink lights"

name: Shadow Art
definition: A pile of random objects that casts a shadow of something totally different, like a heap of junk making the shadow of a dancer.
when_to_use: Use for surprising reveals and clever art pieces. The AI may struggle to match the shadow, so keep the shadow shape simple.
prompt_example: "pile of old shoes casting a shadow of a cat on the wall"

name: Infographic
definition: A clean, friendly layout that explains something with icons, simple charts, arrows and short labels. It looks like a poster you would pin up in a classroom.
when_to_use: Use when you want to explain a process or show facts at a glance. Keep the words few and short, because AI text can still come out scrambled.
prompt_example: "infographic about how bees make honey, flat icons, warm yellow palette"

name: Botanical Plate
definition: An old scientific page showing one plant from root to flower, drawn with care and labeled in small neat writing. Usually soft colors on cream paper, with a few cut-open details on the side.
when_to_use: Use for elegant prints, wall art and anything that should feel studied and calm. Labels may come out as pretend Latin, which often looks charming anyway.
prompt_example: "botanical plate of a wild rose, hand-colored engraving, cream paper"

name: Flowchart
definition: Boxes and arrows that walk you through steps or choices, one after another. Clear, friendly and easy to follow at a glance.
when_to_use: Use for how-to graphics, explainers and playful decision charts. Keep the words short, because AI often scrambles long labels.
prompt_example: "hand-drawn flowchart for choosing a houseplant, pastel boxes and arrows"

name: Blueprint
definition: Crisp white lines on deep blue paper, like an old building plan or machine drawing. Measurements, arrows and grid lines make anything look engineered.
when_to_use: Use to make a design, invention or dream house feel planned and real. Works best for objects and buildings, less well for faces.
prompt_example: "blueprint of a treehouse with rope ladder, white lines on blue"

name: Illuminated Manuscript
definition: A handwritten page from the Middle Ages, glowing with gold leaf, rich colors and a giant decorated first letter. Vines, tiny animals and little figures crawl around the margins.
when_to_use: Use for fantasy, history and anything that should feel sacred or precious. The writing will usually be pretend script, so treat it as decoration.
prompt_example: "illuminated manuscript page of a fox reading a book, gold leaf border"

name: Story Map
definition: An illustrated map that follows one journey, with a winding path and little scenes drawn at each stop along the way. It tells a whole story in one picture.
when_to_use: Use for adventures, children's books, travel memories and event posters. Keep the number of stops small so each scene stays clear.
prompt_example: "story map of a mouse's trip to the sea, winding dotted path, storybook style"

name: Cutaway Diagram
definition: A drawing where a slice of the outside is removed so you can peek inside, like a ship, a house or a volcano cut in half. Every room or layer is on show at once.
when_to_use: Use to show busy little worlds hiding inside something, such as a dollhouse or a submarine. Very detailed scenes can get crowded, so name only a few rooms.
prompt_example: "cutaway diagram of a cozy underground rabbit burrow, every room lit"

name: Field Guide Page
definition: A page from a naturalist's guidebook, with neat painted birds, bugs or mushrooms, each with a small label and notes. It feels patient, curious and outdoorsy.
when_to_use: Use when you want a collection of creatures or plants shown side by side. Great for made-up species too, if you want a gentle fantasy feel.
prompt_example: "field guide page of imaginary forest moths, watercolor, labeled"

name: Spaghetti Western
definition: The dusty Italian-made westerns of the 1960s: squinting eyes in huge close-up, sun-baked desert towns, ponchos and long tense standoffs.
when_to_use: Use for gritty, sweaty, high-noon drama with lots of attitude. Pair with a close-up for that famous staring-down moment.
prompt_example: "spaghetti western standoff, dusty street, extreme close-up of squinting eyes"

name: VHS Horror
definition: Scary movie footage that looks like it was played on a worn-out home video tape. Fuzzy colors, wobbly lines, soft blur and a creepy, homemade feeling.
when_to_use: Use when you want horror that feels found, cheap and a little too real. It hides detail on purpose, so it is not the choice for crisp images.
prompt_example: "vhs horror still, empty hallway at night, tape glitches, washed colors"

name: 90s Sitcom Set
definition: The bright living room of a 90s TV comedy: a big couch facing the camera, a kitchen behind it, flat even lighting and a front door everyone bursts through.
when_to_use: Use for funny, warm, nostalgic scenes where people gather and chat. The flat lighting is part of the charm, so do not expect moody shadows.
prompt_example: "90s sitcom set, friends on a plaid couch, bright studio lighting"

name: Kaiju Film
definition: The classic Japanese giant monster movie: a towering creature stomping through a miniature city, tiny tanks and planes, smoke, sparks and screaming crowds.
when_to_use: Use for big, playful destruction and a sense of huge scale. Add 'miniature set' if you want the handmade, person-in-a-suit charm of the old films.
prompt_example: "kaiju film still, giant lizard monster wading through a toy-like harbor city at night"

name: Telenovela
definition: The glossy Latin American TV drama: grand staircases, gasps, tearful close-ups, big jewelry and secrets revealed in a sunny mansion.
when_to_use: Use when you want over-the-top romance and family drama with lots of feeling. It is meant to be a little much, so lean into it.
prompt_example: "telenovela scene, woman gasping on a marble staircase, dramatic zoom"

name: Silent Film
definition: Old black and white movies from before sound: flickering grain, jerky fast motion, big expressive acting and title cards with fancy borders.
when_to_use: Use for charm, comedy and early 1900s nostalgia. Expect the faces to be exaggerated, because the actors had to tell the story without words.
prompt_example: "silent film still, baker chasing a runaway cake down a street, flickering grain"

name: Wuxia
definition: Chinese martial arts adventure where swordsmen and swordswomen glide across rooftops, bamboo tops and lakes. Flowing robes, misty mountains and graceful, floating fights.
when_to_use: Use for elegant action that feels more like dance than brawling. Great with slow motion and fog for that drifting, weightless look.
prompt_example: "wuxia swordswoman leaping across bamboo treetops, flowing robes, misty valley"

name: Nature Documentary
definition: The patient look of a wildlife film: long lens, soft background, animals going about their day, and the feeling that someone waited hours for this one shot.
when_to_use: Use to make any creature, even a tiny or made-up one, feel real and observed. Works best when the animal looks unaware of the camera.
prompt_example: "nature documentary shot of a fox kit pouncing in snow, telephoto lens"

name: Gothic Novel
definition: The mood of an old Gothic book: crumbling castles, candlelit corridors, storms at the window and a heroine holding a lantern in the dark.
when_to_use: Use for romantic, shivery scenes full of mystery and old stone. Pairs well with candlelight and fog for instant atmosphere.
prompt_example: "gothic novel scene, girl with a lantern on a castle staircase, storm outside"

name: Magical Realism
definition: Everyday life with one quiet impossible thing in it, treated as normal. A grandmother hangs laundry while yellow butterflies follow her, and nobody blinks.
when_to_use: Use when you want gentle wonder inside a real, lived-in place. Keep the magic small and the rest ordinary, or it slides into full fantasy.
prompt_example: "magical realism, old kitchen, woman cooking while flowers grow from the stove"

name: Cozy Mystery
definition: The gentle detective story: a small village, a bookshop or bakery, a cat on the counter and a clue hidden among the teacups. More curious than scary.
when_to_use: Use for warm, charming scenes with a hint of intrigue. Not the choice for real danger or gore, that is the whole point.
prompt_example: "lighthouse keeper's cat, cozy mystery, lamplight"

name: Epic Fantasy Map
definition: The hand-drawn world map at the front of a fantasy novel: mountains drawn as little peaks, winding rivers, sea monsters in the corners and old-style lettering.
when_to_use: Use for worldbuilding, book covers and game art. Place names will often be invented gibberish, so ask for few labels or none.
prompt_example: "epic fantasy map of an island kingdom, ink on parchment, sea serpents"

name: Fairy Tale
definition: The old storybook world of enchanted woods, tiny cottages, talking animals and castles on hills. Soft, a little dark, and full of once upon a time.
when_to_use: Use for magical children's book scenes and dreamy portraits. Add 'dark' if you want the older, stranger versions of these tales.
prompt_example: "fairy tale cottage in a mossy forest, storybook illustration"

name: Penny Dreadful
definition: The cheap, thrilling story papers of Victorian England, full of villains, ghosts and highwaymen. Picture inky woodcut-style illustrations and lurid, shouting headlines.
when_to_use: Use for spooky, sensational Victorian scenes with a printed, pulpy feel. It is rough on purpose, so do not expect polished detail.
prompt_example: "penny dreadful cover, cloaked villain in foggy London alley, woodcut style"

name: Southern Gothic
definition: Stories set in the American South, where the beauty is a little rotten. Peeling mansions, Spanish moss, sticky heat, porch lights and strange, haunted families.
when_to_use: Use for eerie, humid, slow-burning scenes with faded grandeur. Keep it subtle, the spookiness comes from atmosphere, not monsters.
prompt_example: "southern gothic, decaying plantation house, spanish moss, dusk heat haze"

name: Sword and Sorcery
definition: Rough, muscle-and-magic adventure stories: lone warriors, ancient ruins, wicked sorcerers and treasure guarded by something terrible.
when_to_use: Use for bold, painted-paperback fantasy with plenty of action and danger. It is more gritty and personal than grand, kingdom-saving epic fantasy.
prompt_example: "sword and sorcery warrior in a jungle ruin, glowing idol, painted paperback cover"

name: Call to Adventure
definition: The moment just before a journey begins: a letter arrives, a door creaks open, a strange light appears on the hill. The character hasn't moved yet, but everything is about to change.
when_to_use: Use when you want a picture full of possibility and a story waiting to happen. Show the character small and the doorway or path big.
prompt_example: "call to adventure, girl at farmhouse gate, glowing path into the woods"

name: Before and After
definition: One frame split in two, or two moments side by side, showing how something has changed. A bare plot then a full garden, a messy room then a tidy one.
when_to_use: Use to show transformation, growth or the passing of time. Say 'split screen' or 'side by side' clearly, or the model may only show one side.
prompt_example: "before and after, split screen, empty lot and blooming community garden"

name: Reveal
definition: The moment something hidden comes into view: a curtain pulled back, fog lifting from a castle, a face turning toward us. It is all about surprise.
when_to_use: Use for dramatic first looks and big moments. In video this shines with a slow camera move; in a still, show the hiding thing half moved.
prompt_example: "reveal, fog lifting from a giant sleeping dragon in a valley"

name: Quiet Aftermath
definition: The still moment after something big has happened. Confetti on an empty floor, smoke drifting over a field, a tired hero sitting in the dust.
when_to_use: Use when you want feeling without action, letting the viewer imagine what came before. Soft light and empty space make it stronger.
prompt_example: "quiet aftermath, empty ballroom at dawn, fallen streamers, one guest asleep"

name: Calm Before the Storm
definition: A peaceful scene with a hint of trouble on the way: a picnic under darkening clouds, a sleeping town as an army gathers on the hill.
when_to_use: Use to build tension while things still look quiet. Put the calm thing up close and the coming danger small in the distance.
prompt_example: "calm before the storm, kids flying kites, huge black thunderhead behind"

name: Point of No Return
definition: The moment a character commits and can't go back: stepping off the cliff, closing the door behind them, crossing the bridge as it burns.
when_to_use: Use for brave, decisive moments in a story. Show what is being left behind as clearly as where they are going.
prompt_example: "point of no return, knight stepping onto a rope bridge as it frays, back to camera"

name: Homecoming
definition: A traveler arriving back where they started, changed by the journey. Porch lights on, a dog running out, a familiar door seen with new eyes.
when_to_use: Use for warm, emotional endings and reunions. Golden light and a slightly wider shot help it feel like the end of a long story.
prompt_example: "homecoming, tired sailor walking up a lantern-lit path to a cottage, dog running out"

name: Unlikely Friends
definition: Two characters who shouldn't get along, sharing a quiet moment together. A tiny mouse and a huge bear, a knight and a dragon having tea.
when_to_use: Use for heartwarming, funny or gentle storytelling images. The bigger the difference between them, the sweeter it reads.
prompt_example: "unlikely friends, wolf and lamb sharing an umbrella in the rain"

name: Melancholy
definition: A soft, thoughtful sadness, like rain on a window or the last day of summer. Cool, faded colors, lowered eyes and lots of quiet space.
when_to_use: Use when you want an image to feel tender and wistful rather than tragic. Pairs naturally with overcast light and a muted palette.
prompt_example: "melancholy, girl watching rain from a train window, muted colors"

name: Euphoria
definition: Pure, bursting joy: arms thrown wide, heads tipped back laughing, color and light everywhere. The kind of moment you want to live in.
when_to_use: Use for celebrations, music, festivals and big wins. It can tip into chaos, so give it one clear subject to hold onto.
prompt_example: "euphoria, dancers throwing colored powder at sunset festival"

name: Nostalgia
definition: That warm ache for the past: faded photos, sunlit bedrooms, old toys and summer afternoons that seem to last forever.
when_to_use: Use to make a scene feel like a cherished memory. Pairs well with film looks and soft, golden light.
prompt_example: "nostalgia, kids on bikes at dusk, faded film photo, warm light"

name: Awe
definition: The feeling of standing before something enormous and beautiful: a tiny figure under a sky full of stars, a waterfall, a cathedral, a whale.
when_to_use: Use when you want the viewer to feel small in a good way. Make the person tiny and the wonder huge for the biggest effect.
prompt_example: "awe, tiny hiker beneath a vast glowing aurora, snowy peaks"

name: Unease
definition: That quiet feeling that something isn't right. Too-empty rooms, a door left open, a figure standing a little too still at the end of the hall.
when_to_use: Use for gentle creepiness without monsters or gore. Small strange details work better than one big scary thing.
prompt_example: "unease, empty motel corridor at night, one door ajar, flickering light"

name: Longing
definition: Wanting something just out of reach: a face pressed to a window, a hand on a closed door, someone watching a ship sail away.
when_to_use: Use for romantic, hopeful or bittersweet scenes. Put distance or glass between the person and what they want.
prompt_example: "longing, woman on a pier watching a distant ship at dusk, wind in her shawl"

name: Tenderness
definition: Soft, caring closeness: a parent tucking in a child, hands cupping a baby bird, two foreheads touching. Gentle light and gentle gestures.
when_to_use: Use when you want warmth and love without big drama. Close framing and soft light do most of the work.
prompt_example: "tenderness, grandfather tying a little girl's shoelace, soft window light"

name: Defiance
definition: Standing firm against something bigger: chin up, fists clenched, wind in the hair, looking straight back at the storm or the crowd.
when_to_use: Use for brave heroes, protest posters and underdog moments. A low angle makes your subject feel even taller and stronger.
prompt_example: "defiance, young girl facing a giant iron robot, chin raised, rain"

name: Ben-Day Dots
definition: Tiny evenly spaced colored dots used in old printed comics to make pinks, skies and skin tones. Up close they make a bold, poppy pattern.
when_to_use: Use for retro pop art and classic comic looks. Ask for 'large visible dots' if you want them to really show.
prompt_example: "woman crying on a phone, ben-day dots, bold black outlines, pop art"

name: Speech Bubble
definition: The rounded balloon with a little tail that shows who is talking in a comic. Spiky ones shout, cloudy ones think, wobbly ones whisper.
when_to_use: Use to make any image feel like a comic panel. Keep the words to a few, since AI lettering can still come out jumbled.
prompt_example: "cat in a spacesuit, speech bubble saying hello, comic panel"

name: Splash Page
definition: A full comic page given to one huge, dramatic picture, usually a hero arriving or a big battle. No small panels, just one giant moment.
when_to_use: Use for epic, poster-like comic art where everything feels big. Works best with one clear subject and a strong pose.
prompt_example: "splash page, masked heroine landing on a rooftop, city below, dynamic ink"

name: Golden Age Comics
definition: The look of early comic books from the late 1930s to the early 1950s: simple bold heroes, flat bright colors, thick lines and slightly off-register printing on yellowed paper.
when_to_use: Use for retro heroes and charming vintage adventure. The simple style is part of the appeal, so do not expect modern realism.
prompt_example: "golden age comics cover, caped hero lifting a car, flat bright colors, yellowed paper"

name: Sound Effect Lettering
definition: Big, bursting comic words like POW, BOOM and CRASH, drawn in chunky shapes with outlines and jagged edges. The sound becomes part of the picture.
when_to_use: Use for action, comedy and anything loud. Short words work best; longer ones often get misspelled.
prompt_example: "sound effect lettering KABOOM over an exploding birthday cake, comic style"

name: Panel Grid
definition: A page split into neat comic boxes, each showing a moment in order, like a little storyboard. Reading left to right, the story moves along.
when_to_use: Use when you want a short sequence or a mini story in one image. Ask for three or four panels, more often gets confusing.
prompt_example: "four panel grid comic, cat trying to catch a fish, simple ink"

name: Comic Strip
definition: A short row of three or four panels that tells a tiny story, like the funny pages in a Sunday newspaper.
when_to_use: Use for jokes, quick before-and-after stories and character moments. Ask for fewer panels if the faces start to drift between them.
prompt_example: "three-panel comic strip of a cat stealing toast, clean ink lines, bright flat colors"

name: Thought Bubble
definition: A puffy cloud above a character's head, joined by little circles, showing what they are secretly thinking or dreaming.
when_to_use: Use for daydreams, inner jokes and wishes. Describe what is inside the bubble, or AI may leave it empty.
prompt_example: "little girl at a window, thought bubble showing a flying whale"

name: Sherlock Holmes
definition: The sharp-eyed detective from the original stories, tall and thin with a hawk-like nose, as first drawn in old magazine illustrations with a deerstalker cap and travelling cape. Ask for the book version, not later screen versions.
when_to_use: Use for Victorian mysteries, foggy London streets and clever detective portraits. Mention 'Victorian illustration' to keep him true to the books.
prompt_example: "sherlock holmes examining a muddy footprint with a magnifying glass, foggy gaslit london, victorian illustration"

name: Alice in Wonderland
definition: The curious girl who falls down the rabbit hole, as drawn in the original book's pen and ink pictures: long hair, puffed sleeves and a pinafore over her dress. Describe the book version, not later cartoon or film versions.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy, topsy-turvy scenes with odd creatures and impossible tea parties. Say 'Victorian engraving style' for the classic book feel.
prompt_example: "alice in wonderland at a giant tea party, victorian engraving style, mad hatter"

name: Count Dracula
definition: The vampire from the original 1897 novel: a tall old man dressed all in black, with a long white moustache, pointed ears, sharp teeth and hair on his palms. He grows younger as he feeds. Describe the book version, not later film versions.
when_to_use: Use for gothic horror and creepy castle portraits. Asking for the novel's description gives a stranger, fresher look than the usual caped movie vampire.
prompt_example: "count dracula from the 1897 novel, old man in black, long white moustache, candlelit castle stair"

name: Frankenstein's Creature
definition: The being from the 1818 novel: very tall, with yellowish skin, flowing black hair, watery eyes and dark lips, gentle and well-spoken at first. No neck bolts or flat head, those came from later films. Describe the book version.
when_to_use: Use for tragic, thoughtful gothic portraits that feel more human than monster. Say 'as described in the 1818 novel' to steer away from the movie look.
prompt_example: "frankenstein's creature from the 1818 novel, reading by firelight in a snowy hut, melancholy"

name: Little Red Riding Hood
definition: The girl in the red hooded cape from the old fairy tale, carrying a basket through the woods to her grandmother's house while a wolf watches. Describe the classic storybook version.
when_to_use: Use for fairy tale scenes, gentle spookiness and that iconic red against green forest. A bit of fog makes the wolf feel more mysterious.
prompt_example: "little red riding hood on a forest path, wolf eyes in the ferns, storybook illustration"

name: Dorothy of Oz
definition: The Kansas farm girl from the original 1900 book, in a blue and white checked gingham dress with her little dog Toto. In the book her magic shoes are silver, not red. Describe the book version.
when_to_use: Use for whimsical journeys, colorful fantasy lands and yellow brick roads. Mention 'silver shoes' and 'original book illustration' to stay true to the book.
prompt_example: "dorothy of oz from the 1900 book, silver shoes, toto, yellow brick road, original book illustration"

name: Pinocchio
definition: The wooden puppet from the original 1883 Italian story, carved by an old woodcarver, with a nose that grows when he lies. In the book he is a cheeky troublemaker in a paper suit and bark shoes. Describe the book version, not later cartoon versions.
when_to_use: Use for storybook mischief, workshops full of wood shavings and fairy tale lessons. Ask for 'carved wood texture' to keep him a real puppet.
prompt_example: "pinocchio from the 1883 italian story, wooden puppet in a paper suit, cluttered woodcarver's workshop"

name: Captain Nemo
definition: The mysterious captain from the original 1870 novel, who roams the oceans in his submarine, the Nautilus. Picture a proud, bearded man playing an organ in a grand salon with a huge window onto the sea. Describe the book version.
when_to_use: Use for steampunk-flavored undersea adventure and brass-and-velvet interiors. Ask for 'vintage book engraving' for the classic look.
prompt_example: "captain nemo in the nautilus salon, giant round window, glowing jellyfish outside, vintage book engraving"

name: Mid-Leap
definition: Your subject caught in the air at the top of a jump, feet off the ground, everything stretched out. It turns a still picture into a moment of motion.
when_to_use: Use for dancers, athletes, kids and animals full of energy. Hands and feet can get odd in tricky poses, so try a few versions.
prompt_example: "ballet dancer mid-leap over a puddle, city street, golden hour"

name: Twirling
definition: Spinning around with skirts, coats or hair flaring out in a circle. It feels joyful, light and a little romantic.
when_to_use: Use for happy portraits, dresses and dance scenes. A long, flowy outfit makes the motion much easier to see.
prompt_example: "little girl twirling in a yellow dress in a sunflower field"

name: Reaching Out
definition: An arm stretched toward something or someone: a hand reaching for a falling star, a friend, a door, a light. It makes the viewer feel the wanting.
when_to_use: Use for emotional moments of hope, rescue or longing. Show what they are reaching for, or the pose can feel unfinished.
prompt_example: "astronaut reaching out toward a floating flower, deep space glow"

name: Looking Over the Shoulder
definition: Your subject turned away but glancing back toward the camera, as if they just heard their name. It feels candid, mysterious or flirty.
when_to_use: Use for portraits and fashion shots that feel caught in a moment. Lovely with a trailing scarf or loose hair.
prompt_example: "woman looking over the shoulder at a rainy paris crosswalk, red umbrella"

name: Tiptoeing
definition: Creeping along on the very tips of the toes, shoulders hunched, trying not to make a sound. Instantly sneaky and funny.
when_to_use: Use for playful mischief, cartoon sneaking and bedtime scenes. Add a sleeping pet or parent to show what they are sneaking past.
prompt_example: "small boy tiptoeing past a sleeping dog toward the cookie jar, night kitchen"

name: Mid-Laugh
definition: Caught in the middle of a real laugh, eyes squeezed, head tipped back, maybe a hand over the mouth. Natural joy that feels unposed.
when_to_use: Use when stiff smiling portraits feel fake. Teeth and eyes can look a bit strange up close, so a slightly wider shot often helps.
prompt_example: "two old friends mid-laugh at a diner booth, candid film photo"

name: Running Toward Camera
definition: Your subject racing straight at the viewer, hair and clothes flying, getting bigger in the frame. It pulls you right into the action.
when_to_use: Use for chases, joyful reunions and big action. It is strongest in video; in a still image, add motion blur so it doesn't look frozen.
prompt_example: "kids running toward camera through a sprinkler, summer afternoon, slow motion"

name: Falling Backward
definition: A body tipping back into the air, arms loose, as if falling into water, a bed of flowers or a dream. It feels like letting go.
when_to_use: Use for surreal, dreamy and trust-falling moments. Show what they are falling into, so it reads as peaceful rather than scary.
prompt_example: "woman falling backward into a pool of floating petals, overhead view"

name: 1920s Flapper Dress
definition: Loose, straight dresses that drop to the hips and stop near the knee, covered in beads, sequins or swinging fringe. Think bobbed hair, long pearls and a feathered headband.
when_to_use: Use for jazz age parties, speakeasies and dance scenes. Fringe and beads come alive in video when the dancer moves.
prompt_example: "woman in a beaded 1920s flapper dress, art deco ballroom"

name: Regency Era Fashion
definition: Early 1800s dress with a waistline just under the bust, light white muslin falling straight to the floor, short puffed sleeves, bonnets and little cropped jackets.
when_to_use: Use for period romance, country house scenes and garden walks. Say "empire waist" too if the waistline keeps slipping down.
prompt_example: "young woman in a white regency era muslin gown, walking through an english garden"

name: Edwardian Fashion
definition: Dress from the early 1900s: high lace collars, puffy blouses, long sweeping skirts and enormous hats piled with flowers and feathers. Elegant, layered and very ladylike.
when_to_use: Use for garden parties, grand hotels and early 1900s city streets. It can blur into Victorian, so add the decade if you need it exact.
prompt_example: "edwardian fashion, woman in a lace blouse and wide feathered hat, seaside promenade, 1905"

name: 1950s New Look
definition: The postwar silhouette made famous by Christian Dior: soft rounded shoulders, a tiny cinched waist and a full skirt that swings below the knee. Polished, feminine and very structured.
when_to_use: Use for 1950s glamour, diners, garden parties and vintage ads. Add gloves, a hat or a petticoat for even more period detail.
prompt_example: "woman in a 1950s new look dress with a full skirt and cinched waist, paris street"

name: 1970s Disco Fashion
definition: Shiny, flowing clothes made for the dance floor: halter jumpsuits, wrap dresses, wide bell bottoms, platform shoes and gold or silver metallic fabric that catches every light.
when_to_use: Use for nightclub scenes, mirror balls and dance videos. Pair it with colored light so the shine has something to reflect.
prompt_example: "dancers in 1970s disco fashion, metallic halter jumpsuits, mirror ball light"

name: 1960s Mod Fashion
definition: The bold London look of the mid 1960s: short shift dresses, mini skirts, bright color blocks, black and white graphics, go-go boots and sharp geometric haircuts.
when_to_use: Use for playful, graphic fashion with a youthful swagger. Works best with clean, simple backgrounds that let the shapes pop.
prompt_example: "model in a 1960s mod fashion mini dress with black and white stripes, white go-go boots"

name: 1940s Wartime Fashion
definition: Practical style shaped by fabric rationing: padded shoulders, knee-length skirts, neat tailored jackets, headscarves and pinned-up victory roll hairstyles.
when_to_use: Use for World War II era home front scenes, factories, train stations and letters home. Add the setting so it does not drift into the 1950s.
prompt_example: "woman in 1940s wartime fashion, padded shoulder jacket and headscarf, railway station"

name: Elizabethan Fashion
definition: English court dress from the late 1500s: huge starched lace ruffs around the neck, stiff jeweled bodices, wide skirts held out by hoops, and rich brocade sewn with pearls.
when_to_use: Use for royal portraits, historical drama and Shakespeare-style scenes. Very ornate, so keep the rest of the scene simple.
prompt_example: "portrait of a noblewoman in elizabethan fashion, white lace ruff, pearl-studded gown"

name: Hanbok
definition: Traditional Korean clothing. For women, a short jacket called a jeogori over a full, high-waisted skirt called a chima; for men, a jacket with roomy trousers. Soft colors and graceful lines.
when_to_use: Use for Korean family celebrations and portraits. Hanbok is worn for special days like Seollal, Chuseok, a baby's first birthday and weddings, so show it with that care.
prompt_example: "young woman in a pastel pink hanbok, palace courtyard in autumn"

name: Kimono
definition: Japan's traditional robe: a straight, T-shaped garment wrapped around the body and tied with a wide sash called an obi. Fabrics range from simple cotton to silk painted with flowers and cranes.
when_to_use: Use for Japanese gardens, tea ceremonies and festivals. Kimono wrap left side over right; right over left is reserved for dressing the deceased, so check your results.
prompt_example: "woman in a silk kimono with crane pattern, kyoto garden, morning light"

name: Sari
definition: A long, unstitched length of cloth, usually five to nine yards, draped around the body over a fitted blouse, with the decorated end falling over the shoulder. Worn across South Asia in many regional styles.
when_to_use: Use for everyday portraits, festivals and weddings. Richly woven silk saris, often red, are bridal wear in many regions, so name the occasion and color you want.
prompt_example: "woman in a deep red silk sari with gold border, marigold garlands, warm evening light"

name: Kente Cloth
definition: Brightly colored cloth from Ghana, made by the Asante and Ewe peoples by weaving narrow strips on a loom and sewing them together. Bold blocks of gold, green, red and black, each pattern with its own name and meaning.
when_to_use: Use for celebrations, portraits and graduation scenes. Kente was once reserved for royalty and is still worn for important ceremonies, so treat it as a meaningful cloth, not a random pattern.
prompt_example: "graduate wearing a kente cloth stole, proud smile, sunny campus lawn"

name: Dashiki
definition: A loose, colorful pullover tunic from West Africa with a richly embroidered or printed neckline. Comfortable, roomy and full of bold color.
when_to_use: Use for portraits, family gatherings and festival scenes. In the 1960s it also became a proud symbol of Black identity in the United States, which can add meaning to your scene.
prompt_example: "man in a bright blue dashiki with gold embroidered neckline, outdoor market"

name: Huipil
definition: A loose tunic made from rectangles of handwoven cloth, worn by Indigenous women in southern Mexico and Guatemala. Covered in woven and embroidered flowers, birds and geometric bands.
when_to_use: Use for portraits and market scenes with real cultural detail. Designs often tell which town or community the weaver comes from, and some huipiles are made only for ceremonies.
prompt_example: "woman weaving on a backstrap loom, wearing an embroidered huipil, guatemalan highlands"

name: Ao Dai
definition: Vietnam's national dress: a long, fitted silk tunic with a high collar and side slits up to the waist, worn over loose flowing trousers. Simple, slim and graceful.
when_to_use: Use for portraits, city streets and Lunar New Year scenes. Ao dai is worn for Tet, weddings and as a school uniform, and the long panels look lovely moving in the wind.
prompt_example: "woman in a white ao dai cycling past a hanoi lake, morning mist"

name: Qipao
definition: A fitted Chinese dress with a high mandarin collar, side slits and frog-knot buttons, often in silk with embroidered flowers. Also called a cheongsam.
when_to_use: Use for elegant portraits and 1930s Shanghai scenes. It is worn for weddings and Lunar New Year, so treat it as special dress, not a costume.
prompt_example: "woman in a red silk qipao, 1930s Shanghai street, soft evening light"

name: Plus-Size
definition: A fuller, larger body shown naturally and confidently. AI tends to slim everyone down by default, so this word helps it show the many people who wear larger sizes.
when_to_use: Use whenever you want real, everyday representation in fashion, lifestyle and portrait scenes. Pair it with clothing and an activity so the person is the story, not their size.
prompt_example: "plus-size woman laughing with friends at a picnic, linen dress, sunny park"

name: Petite
definition: A shorter, small-framed body. Clothes and furniture look a little bigger around them, and they read clearly as an adult, not a child.
when_to_use: Use to show shorter adults in fashion, office and everyday scenes. Add an age or role, like "petite woman in her forties", so the AI keeps them grown up.
prompt_example: "petite woman in her forties in a tailored blazer, city crosswalk"

name: Tall and Lanky
definition: A long, thin body with long arms and legs, often a little gangly. They tower over the crowd and have to duck through doorways.
when_to_use: Use for characters with height as a natural part of who they are, from teen athletes to quiet bookworms. Add a scale clue, like a doorway or other people, so the height shows.
prompt_example: "tall and lanky young man ducking under a low cafe doorway, warm afternoon"

name: Athletic Build
definition: A strong, fit body with visible muscle from sport or training. Shoulders, arms and legs look capable and ready to move.
when_to_use: Use for sports, fitness and action scenes for any age or gender. If results look like bodybuilders, say "lean athletic build" or name the sport.
prompt_example: "woman with an athletic build tying her running shoes, misty track at dawn"

name: Broad-Shouldered
definition: Wide shoulders and a sturdy upper body, the kind of frame that fills a doorway or a jacket. Reads strong, solid and dependable.
when_to_use: Use for builders, rowers, swimmers or anyone with a strong frame, of any gender. Helps break the AI habit of giving everyone the same narrow shape.
prompt_example: "broad-shouldered woman carrying lumber on a building site, golden hour"

name: Elderly
definition: An older person, often in their seventies or beyond, with lined skin, silver or thinning hair and hands that show a long life. Shown with dignity, warmth and character.
when_to_use: Use to bring older people into your scenes as full, active people: gardeners, dancers, teachers, grandparents. Name an activity so they are doing, not just sitting.
prompt_example: "elderly man with silver beard tending tomatoes in a sunny allotment"

name: Stocky Build
definition: A short to medium height body that is solid, thick-set and sturdy, with a strong chest and wide stance. Grounded and powerful rather than tall.
when_to_use: Use for blacksmiths, chefs, farmers, wrestlers or any character who should feel solid and steady. Works for all genders.
prompt_example: "stocky blacksmith with a leather apron at a glowing forge"

name: Average Build
definition: An ordinary, everyday body: not model-thin, not bulky, just the shape most people actually have. Soft in some places, firm in others.
when_to_use: Use when the AI keeps giving you glossy, perfect bodies and you want real people. Great for lifestyle and stock-style scenes that need to feel relatable.
prompt_example: "man with an average build making pancakes in a sunlit kitchen, sweatpants and t-shirt"

name: Tailored Suit
definition: A jacket and trousers cut to fit the body just right, with crisp shoulders, clean lines and no extra fabric. Smart, sharp and pulled together.
when_to_use: Use for professional portraits, weddings and confident characters of any gender. Add a fabric, like wool or linen, and a color for more control.
prompt_example: "man in a navy tailored suit, standing by a tall office window"

name: Oversized Streetwear
definition: Baggy hoodies, roomy cargo pants, big puffer jackets and chunky sneakers, worn loose and layered. Relaxed, cool and very city.
when_to_use: Use for urban portraits, skate parks and music videos. Avoid brand names; describe colors and pieces instead.
prompt_example: "teen in oversized streetwear, baggy hoodie and cargo pants, graffiti alley"

name: Quiet Luxury
definition: Simple, expensive-looking clothes with no logos: cashmere knits, camel coats, soft trousers and perfect fit in cream, beige and grey. Rich without shouting about it.
when_to_use: Use for calm, upscale lifestyle and fashion images. It can look plain in a busy scene, so give it a clean, airy setting.
prompt_example: "woman in a cream cashmere sweater and camel coat, minimal sunlit apartment"

name: Cottage Dress
definition: A soft, romantic dress with puffed sleeves, a fitted bodice and tiny floral print, often in cotton or linen. Feels like picking wildflowers and baking bread.
when_to_use: Use for countryside, picnic and garden scenes with a gentle, storybook mood. Pairs naturally with baskets, meadows and golden light.
prompt_example: "girl in a floral cottage dress with puffed sleeves, wildflower meadow"

name: Power Suit
definition: A bold suit made to command a room: strong padded shoulders, sharp lapels and a confident color like red, white or black. Very 1980s boardroom, still powerful today.
when_to_use: Use for leaders, bosses and confident portraits of any gender. Push it with a low angle for extra authority.
prompt_example: "woman in a red power suit with strong shoulders, glass boardroom"

name: Athleisure
definition: Sporty clothes worn as everyday wear: leggings, joggers, zip-up tops, soft hoodies and clean sneakers. Comfy, fresh and ready for anything.
when_to_use: Use for lifestyle, coffee runs, yoga and wellness scenes. Describe colors and fabrics instead of brand names.
prompt_example: "friends in matching sage green athleisure walking with coffee, morning city street"

name: Boho Chic
definition: Free-spirited, layered style: flowing maxi skirts, fringed suede, embroidered tops, wide-brim hats and stacks of jewelry. Earthy, relaxed and a little wild.
when_to_use: Use for festivals, desert road trips and sunny outdoor portraits. Pairs well with warm, dusty light and natural textures.
prompt_example: "woman in boho chic outfit, fringed suede vest and maxi skirt, desert at sunset"

name: Monochrome Outfit
definition: An outfit in a single color from head to toe, like all camel, all lilac or all black, mixing different shades and textures of that one color.
when_to_use: Use for striking fashion images and clean product shots. Name the color clearly, and a matching background makes it even bolder.
prompt_example: "model in an all lilac monochrome outfit against a lilac backdrop"

name: Coco Chanel
definition: French designer Coco Chanel (1883-1971) freed women from corsets with comfortable jersey, collarless tweed suits trimmed in braid, the little black dress and long ropes of pearls.
when_to_use: Use for chic, timeless Parisian elegance in black, white and cream. It points to her classic look, so describe the outfit if you want something modern.
prompt_example: "woman in a cream tweed suit with braid trim and pearls, in the style of coco chanel, paris apartment"

name: Christian Dior
definition: French designer Christian Dior (1905-1957) launched the 1947 New Look: soft shoulders, tiny cinched waists and huge full skirts that brought romance back after the war.
when_to_use: Use for 1950s couture glamour and dramatic ball gowns. Great with fashion photo terms for a vintage magazine feel.
prompt_example: "evening gown in the style of christian dior, full tulle skirt, cinched waist, 1950s couture salon"

name: Cristobal Balenciaga
definition: Spanish designer Cristóbal Balenciaga (1895-1972) shaped fabric like sculpture: balloon skirts, cocoon coats, loose sack dresses and stiff silks that stand away from the body.
when_to_use: Use when you want bold, architectural shapes and simple, strong colors. Works best on a plain background where the silhouette can speak.
prompt_example: "sculptural cocoon coat in the style of cristobal balenciaga, black silk, plain grey studio"

name: Elsa Schiaparelli
definition: Italian-born designer Elsa Schiaparelli (1890-1973) made fashion playful and surreal: shocking pink, trick-of-the-eye sweaters, lobster prints, hats shaped like shoes and wild jeweled buttons.
when_to_use: Use for witty, dreamlike fashion that breaks the rules. Add one surreal detail to the prompt so the AI knows where to play.
prompt_example: "surreal evening gown in the style of elsa schiaparelli, shocking pink, lobster print, gilded salon"

name: Yves Saint Laurent
definition: French designer Yves Saint Laurent (1936-2008) put women in tuxedos with his famous Le Smoking suit, and loved safari jackets, sheer blouses and bold blocks of color inspired by art.
when_to_use: Use for confident, sleek 1960s and 1970s Parisian style. Great for tuxedo looks and dramatic black and white fashion portraits.
prompt_example: "woman in a black tuxedo suit in the style of yves saint laurent, paris street at night"

name: Alexander McQueen
definition: British designer Alexander McQueen (1969-2010) mixed razor-sharp tailoring with dark, romantic drama: tartan, feathers, lace, skulls and runway shows that felt like theater.
when_to_use: Use for dramatic, gothic and haunting fashion. It can tip into spooky fast, so add color words if you want it lighter.
prompt_example: "gown of black feathers and red tartan in the style of alexander mcqueen, misty moor"

name: Madeleine Vionnet
definition: French designer Madeleine Vionnet (1876-1975) mastered the bias cut, cutting fabric on the diagonal so silk gowns drape, cling and flow like water, often with a Greek statue feel.
when_to_use: Use for liquid, flowing evening gowns and 1930s Hollywood-style elegance. Pairs beautifully with soft light that shows the folds.
prompt_example: "flowing bias-cut silk gown in the style of madeleine vionnet, pale champagne, marble hall"

name: Halston
definition: American designer Halston (1932-1990) defined 1970s glamour with simple, fluid pieces: jersey halter gowns, caftans, wrap shapes and clean minimal lines that moved on the dance floor.
when_to_use: Use for sleek 1970s nightlife and minimalist evening wear. Great with disco light, but keep the clothes simple to stay true to him.
prompt_example: "flowing red jersey halter gown in the style of halston, 1970s nightclub, mirror ball"

name: Opal
definition: A milky or dark gemstone that flashes little patches of rainbow color as it moves, like fire trapped inside. No two look the same.
when_to_use: Use for magical, dreamy jewelry and fantasy treasure. Close-ups show the color play best; small stones in wide shots can turn plain white.
prompt_example: "opal ring flashing blue and green fire, macro shot on black velvet"

name: Emerald Cut
definition: A rectangle-shaped gem cut with clipped corners and long, step-like facets. Instead of sparkle, it gives clean flashes of light like a hall of mirrors.
when_to_use: Use for elegant, vintage-feeling rings and pendants, with any stone, not just emeralds. Say the stone and the setting for best results.
prompt_example: "emerald cut diamond engagement ring, platinum setting, soft window light"

name: Filigree
definition: Jewelry made from tiny twisted threads of gold or silver, curled into delicate lace-like patterns full of little open spaces.
when_to_use: Use for heirloom, fantasy and wedding jewelry with lots of fine detail. Works best in close-up; very small filigree can turn to mush.
prompt_example: "silver filigree earrings with tiny swirls and loops, close-up on linen"

name: Art Nouveau Jewelry
definition: Jewelry from around 1890 to 1910 full of flowing curves: dragonflies, orchids, peacock feathers and women with long hair, often in glowing enamel, opal and gold.
when_to_use: Use for romantic, nature-inspired jewelry and fantasy accessories. The flowing lines also pair nicely with stained glass and botanical scenes.
prompt_example: "art nouveau jewelry brooch, enamel dragonfly with opal wings, gold"

name: Pearls
definition: Smooth, round gems grown inside oysters and mussels, with a soft, glowing shine. They come in white, cream, pink, gold and dark grey, and in lumpy shapes called baroque pearls.
when_to_use: Use for classic elegance on necklaces, earrings and hair pieces. Add "baroque pearls" for irregular shapes with a more artistic feel.
prompt_example: "woman wearing a long strand of cream pearls, black dress, soft studio light"

name: Rose Gold
definition: Gold mixed with copper to give a warm, pinkish blush color. Softer and more romantic than yellow gold.
when_to_use: Use for jewelry, watches and product shots with a warm, modern, gentle feel. Pairs nicely with pastel backgrounds.
prompt_example: "rose gold bangle with tiny diamonds on blush pink silk"

name: Cabochon
definition: A gemstone polished into a smooth, rounded dome with no sharp facets. It glows from within instead of sparkling.
when_to_use: Use for vintage, medieval and fantasy jewelry, especially with moonstone, turquoise or garnet. Great for rings that look old and treasured.
prompt_example: "antique gold ring with a deep red garnet cabochon, candlelit wooden table"

name: Turquoise
definition: A sky-blue to green stone, often with dark web-like veins running through it. Loved for centuries in jewelry from Persia, Tibet and the American Southwest.
when_to_use: Use for bold silver jewelry, desert styling and earthy color accents. Name the culture or style you want, since turquoise traditions are rich and specific.
prompt_example: "chunky silver cuff bracelet set with turquoise stones, desert sand, warm light"

name: Corporate Headshot
definition: A clean, friendly head and shoulders portrait on a plain or softly blurred background, with even, flattering light and a confident smile.
when_to_use: Use for team pages, profile pictures and speaker bios. Add an age, outfit and background color so every headshot doesn't look the same.
prompt_example: "corporate headshot of a woman in a grey blazer, soft grey backdrop, friendly smile"
pairs_well_with: soft key;shallow depth of field;tailored suit

name: Open-Plan Office
definition: A big, bright office with no walls between desks: long tables, laptops, plants, big windows and people working side by side.
when_to_use: Use for company websites, hiring pages and work culture scenes. Ask for candid, real people to avoid stiff stock-photo poses.
prompt_example: "open-plan office with plants and big windows, team working at long desks, morning light"

name: Boardroom
definition: A formal meeting room with a long polished table, rows of chairs, a big screen and often a city view behind glass walls.
when_to_use: Use for leadership, big decisions and serious business moments. Add people and a mood, or it can feel cold and empty.
prompt_example: "executives around a long boardroom table at dusk, city lights through glass walls"

name: Startup Garage
definition: A scrappy workspace in a home garage: folding tables, laptops, tangled cables, whiteboards and pizza boxes. Big dreams, tiny budget.
when_to_use: Use for founder stories, origin moments and humble beginnings. Warm, practical lamp light makes it feel hopeful.
prompt_example: "two founders working late in a cluttered startup garage, laptops and whiteboard, warm lamp light"

name: Product Mockup
definition: A clean, realistic picture showing a product, package or screen design in a real setting, like a box on a table or an app on a phone in someone's hand.
when_to_use: Use to preview packaging, labels and app screens before they exist. AI often garbles small text, so add real lettering afterward in a design app.
prompt_example: "product mockup of a plain kraft paper coffee bag on a marble counter, soft daylight"
pairs_well_with: soft key;shallow depth of field;macro photography

name: SaaS Flat Illustration
definition: Friendly, simple vector drawings used on software websites: flat colors, rounded people with no fine detail, floating charts, cloud icons and laptops.
when_to_use: Use for websites, onboarding screens and explainer graphics. It can feel generic, so pick a brand-like color palette to make it yours.
prompt_example: "saas flat illustration of a team building a dashboard together, purple and teal palette, white background"

name: Coworking Space
definition: A shared, stylish workspace where freelancers and small teams rent desks: exposed brick, cozy sofas, phone booths, coffee bar and lots of plants.
when_to_use: Use for freelance life, networking and creative work scenes. Name a mood like cozy or busy to set the energy.
prompt_example: "freelancers working in a coworking space with exposed brick and plants, afternoon sun"

name: Whiteboard Brainstorm
definition: A team gathered around a whiteboard covered in sticky notes, arrows and quick sketches, pointing and thinking out loud.
when_to_use: Use for teamwork, planning and creative problem-solving images. Writing on the board will usually be gibberish, so keep it in soft focus or crop it out.
prompt_example: "diverse team in a whiteboard brainstorm, colorful sticky notes, bright meeting room"

name: Textbook Illustration
definition: Clear, carefully labeled drawings like the ones in school science and history books: cutaway views, neat arrows and calm, flat colors.
when_to_use: Use for explaining how things work, from volcanoes to the water cycle. Labels often come out as nonsense words, so plan to add real text later.
prompt_example: "textbook illustration of a volcano cutaway with labeled layers, clean flat colors"

name: Lab Notebook
definition: A scientist's working notebook: grid paper filled with handwritten notes, quick sketches, taped-in photos, coffee rings and crossed-out numbers.
when_to_use: Use for science stories, research moods and backgrounds with a hands-on feel. Handwriting will be decorative, not readable.
prompt_example: "open lab notebook on a bench, handwritten notes and sketches of molecules, glass beakers nearby"

name: Chalkboard Lecture
definition: A teacher at a big chalkboard covered in dusty white equations, diagrams and arrows, with chalk smudges and a classroom full of attention.
when_to_use: Use for teaching, science and math moments, and the classic "genius at work" scene. Equations will look real from afar but won't make sense up close.
prompt_example: "professor writing equations at a chalkboard lecture, chalk dust in a sunbeam"

name: Scientific Poster
definition: The big printed poster researchers pin up at conferences: a title banner across the top, neat columns, charts, photos and small blocks of text.
when_to_use: Use for research mockups, school projects and conference scenes. AI can't write accurate science text, so treat it as a layout idea and fill in real words yourself.
prompt_example: "scientific poster about coral reefs, title banner, charts and photos in neat columns"

name: Library Study
definition: Quiet hours in a grand library: long wooden tables, green reading lamps, tall shelves of old books and a student lost in their notes.
when_to_use: Use for studying, research and calm, focused moods. Lovely for cozy video loops with drifting dust and turning pages.
prompt_example: "student taking notes at a long table in a library study, green reading lamps, tall shelves"

name: Anatomical Drawing
definition: Old-style scientific drawings of the human body or animals, showing bones, muscles and organs in fine ink lines, often on yellowed paper with little labels.
when_to_use: Use for vintage science art, medical themes and curiosity-cabinet looks. Keep it to clean study drawings rather than anything gory.
prompt_example: "antique anatomical drawing of a human hand showing bones and tendons, ink on aged paper"

name: Lecture Hall
definition: A big university room with rows of seats rising in tiers toward the back, a lectern and screen at the front, and students listening or taking notes.
when_to_use: Use for university life, talks and learning scenes. A wide shot from the back shows the scale best.
prompt_example: "wide view of a lecture hall from the back row, students with laptops, professor at a lectern"

name: Naturalist Field Journal
definition: A nature explorer's sketchbook: watercolor studies of birds, leaves and insects, handwritten notes, pressed flowers and dates in the margins.
when_to_use: Use for nature study, cozy adventure and science-meets-art pages. Lovely with watercolor and botanical styles; the writing is decorative only.
prompt_example: "naturalist field journal page with watercolor sketches of birds and pressed ferns, handwritten notes"

name: Frank Lloyd Wright
definition: American architect (1867-1959) whose houses hug the land with long, low roofs, warm wood, stone and bands of windows. His most famous home sits right over a waterfall.
when_to_use: Use for calm, earthy homes that feel grown from the landscape. Works best for houses and cabins, less so for city towers.
prompt_example: "house built over a forest waterfall, Frank Lloyd Wright style, autumn"

name: Antoni Gaudi
definition: Spanish architect (1852-1926) whose buildings look like they melted, sprouted or grew from the sea. Wavy walls, bone-shaped columns and broken tile mosaics in every color.
when_to_use: Use when you want a building that feels alive and dreamlike. It can get busy fast, so keep the rest of the prompt simple.
prompt_example: "cathedral interior like a stone forest, Antoni Gaudi style, colored light"

name: Zaha Hadid
definition: Iraqi-British architect (1950-2016) known for buildings that swoop and flow like liquid, with no straight corners. Smooth white curves that look like they are in motion.
when_to_use: Use for sleek, futuristic buildings and spaces that feel fast even standing still. Too much of it can look like a generic sci-fi set, so add a real place or material.
prompt_example: "opera house of flowing white curves at dusk, Zaha Hadid style"

name: Le Corbusier
definition: Swiss-French architect (1887-1965) who made clean white boxes lifted on slim pillars, with long strip windows and flat roof gardens. Later work used chunky raw concrete.
when_to_use: Use for crisp early modern homes and bold concrete housing blocks. Can look cold, so warm it up with sunlight or plants.
prompt_example: "white villa raised on thin pillars, Le Corbusier style, summer lawn"

name: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
definition: German-American architect (1886-1969) famous for the motto 'less is more.' Glass walls, thin steel frames and open floors so simple they almost disappear.
when_to_use: Use for quiet, elegant glass pavilions and towers. There is not much ornament here, so the light and setting do the work.
prompt_example: "glass house in a snowy meadow, Mies van der Rohe style, morning light"

name: Oscar Niemeyer
definition: Brazilian architect (1907-2012) who bent white concrete into sweeping curves, domes and bowls. His buildings look like sculptures floating on reflecting pools.
when_to_use: Use for bright, graceful modern buildings with a tropical, optimistic feel. Pairs beautifully with big skies and water.
prompt_example: "curved white concrete chapel by a lake, Oscar Niemeyer style, blue sky"

name: Louis Kahn
definition: American architect (1901-1974) whose buildings feel like ancient monuments: massive concrete and brick walls, perfect circles and squares, and light pouring through huge cut-out openings.
when_to_use: Use for serious, temple-like spaces full of shadow and sunbeams. Not the right pick for cozy or playful scenes.
prompt_example: "concrete courtyard facing the ocean, Louis Kahn style, late afternoon"

name: Luis Barragan
definition: Mexican architect (1902-1988) known for smooth walls painted hot pink, sunny yellow and deep blue, with still pools of water and sharp shadows. Simple shapes, bold color, total calm.
when_to_use: Use for sunny, colorful courtyards and walls that photograph like paintings. Keep the scene uncluttered so the colors can sing.
prompt_example: "pink courtyard wall with a still pool, Luis Barragan style, midday sun"

name: Bauhaus
definition: Early 1900s German modern style built from simple boxes, flat roofs, big windows and no decoration. Often white walls with pops of red, yellow and blue.
when_to_use: Use for clean, honest buildings and graphic, geometric scenes. It is very plain on purpose, so add color or people if it feels empty.
prompt_example: "white Bauhaus apartment block, red door, sunny morning"

name: Mid-Century Modern
definition: The look of 1950s and 60s homes: low flat roofs, walls of glass, warm wood and open rooms that flow out to the garden.
when_to_use: Use for stylish, sunny homes with a relaxed retro feel. One of the easiest styles to get right in any model.
prompt_example: "mid-century modern house with a pool, palm trees, golden hour"

name: Art Nouveau Architecture
definition: Buildings from around 1900 covered in flowing, plant-like curves: whiplash ironwork, flower-shaped windows and doorways that look like vines.
when_to_use: Use for romantic, storybook city buildings and metro entrances. Adds lots of detail, so it shines in close or medium views.
prompt_example: "Art Nouveau cafe facade with curling iron vines, rainy evening"

name: Moorish Architecture
definition: Palaces and courtyards from Islamic Spain and North Africa, with horseshoe arches, carved plaster lace, patterned tiles and quiet fountains.
when_to_use: Use for rich, peaceful courtyards and palace halls full of pattern. Be respectful and specific about place when it matters to your story.
prompt_example: "Moorish courtyard with horseshoe arches and a tiled fountain, soft afternoon light"

name: Craftsman Bungalow
definition: A cozy early 1900s American house with a low roof, a deep front porch on thick tapered columns, and lots of natural wood and stone.
when_to_use: Use for warm, welcoming small homes and neighborhood streets. Great for nostalgic, family-feeling scenes.
prompt_example: "Craftsman bungalow with a lantern-lit porch, autumn leaves, dusk"

name: Mediterranean Villa
definition: Sun-washed white or warm plaster walls, red clay roof tiles, arched windows, terraces and bright flowers spilling over stone steps.
when_to_use: Use for holiday, summer and seaside dream homes. Pairs naturally with blue sea and strong sun.
prompt_example: "Mediterranean villa on a cliff, bougainvillea, sea view, late afternoon"

name: Googie
definition: Space age roadside style from 1950s America: boomerang roofs, starbursts, tilted glass and big neon signs on diners, motels and car washes.
when_to_use: Use for fun retro diners, motels and atomic age streets. It reads strongly American, so lean into it.
prompt_example: "Googie diner with a boomerang roof and neon sign, desert night"

name: Tudor Revival
definition: Storybook houses with dark wooden beams crossing white walls, steep pointed roofs, tall chimneys and small diamond-paned windows.
when_to_use: Use for fairytale villages, English cottages and cozy old manor houses. Can look like a theme park if everything is too clean, so add age.
prompt_example: "Tudor Revival cottage with ivy, misty morning, village lane"

name: Japandi
definition: A calm mix of Japanese and Scandinavian rooms: low wood furniture, linen, paper lamps, soft beige and gray, and almost no clutter.
when_to_use: Use for peaceful, airy rooms that feel like a deep breath. If you want color or personality, this is the wrong word.
prompt_example: "reading nook, Japandi interior, morning light"

name: Maximalist Interior
definition: More is more: layered patterns, bold wallpaper, stacks of books, plants, art covering every wall and bright clashing colors that somehow work.
when_to_use: Use for joyful, personality-packed rooms full of things to look at. Can turn into visual noise, so name two or three main colors.
prompt_example: "maximalist living room, jungle wallpaper, velvet sofa, gallery wall"

name: Scandinavian Interior
definition: Bright white walls, pale wood floors, simple furniture, cozy wool throws and plenty of daylight. Clean and homey at the same time.
when_to_use: Use for fresh, light, lived-in rooms. A safe, friendly default that rarely goes wrong.
prompt_example: "Scandinavian interior kitchen, white walls, birch table, winter daylight"

name: Boho Interior
definition: Free-spirited rooms with rattan, woven rugs, macrame, floor cushions, trailing plants and warm earthy colors.
when_to_use: Use for relaxed, sunny, traveler-style spaces. Easy to overdo, so pick a few hero pieces.
prompt_example: "boho interior bedroom, macrame wall hanging, rattan peacock chair, plants"

name: Hollywood Regency
definition: Old Hollywood glamour at home: glossy lacquer, mirrored furniture, gold accents, bold black and white, and jewel-colored velvet.
when_to_use: Use for glamorous, a little theatrical rooms with movie star energy. Too much gold can look cheap, so balance it with black or white.
prompt_example: "Hollywood Regency dressing room, mirrored vanity, emerald velvet, gold lamps"

name: Modern Farmhouse
definition: White walls, wooden beams, shiplap boards, a big farm sink and black metal lights. Country charm, kept clean and simple.
when_to_use: Use for warm family kitchens and homey living rooms. It is very familiar, so add one surprise to keep it from feeling generic.
prompt_example: "modern farmhouse kitchen, wood beams, farm sink, morning light"

name: English Country House
definition: Faded chintz sofas, floral curtains, worn rugs, dogs by the fire, oil portraits and piles of books. Comfortable, a bit shabby and full of history.
when_to_use: Use for cozy old manor rooms that feel lived in for generations. Best when things look slightly worn rather than brand new.
prompt_example: "English country house drawing room, chintz sofa, fireplace, rainy afternoon"

name: Industrial Loft
definition: Old factory space turned home: exposed brick, steel beams, giant windows, concrete floors and pipes left showing.
when_to_use: Use for creative city apartments, studios and moody urban scenes. Can feel cold, so add warm lamps or leather.
prompt_example: "industrial loft apartment, exposed brick, tall steel windows, evening"

name: Elsie de Wolfe
definition: American decorator (1859-1950) often called the first professional interior designer. She swapped dark Victorian rooms for light walls, mirrors, garden trellis and pretty chintz.
when_to_use: Use for airy, feminine, garden-inspired rooms with an early 1900s feel. Keeps things soft and fresh rather than grand.
prompt_example: "sunroom with green trellis walls and chintz chairs, Elsie de Wolfe style"

name: Dorothy Draper
definition: American decorator (1889-1969) known for big, happy glamour: black and white checkerboard floors, huge cabbage rose prints, bright pink and green, and giant white plaster scrolls.
when_to_use: Use for bold, cheerful hotel lobbies and dramatic rooms. Not for minimal or quiet scenes.
prompt_example: "hotel lobby, black and white checkered floor, pink and green walls, Dorothy Draper style"

name: Billy Baldwin
definition: American decorator (1903-1983) known for glossy chocolate brown walls, tall brass bookshelves, simple cotton slipcovers and comfy slipper chairs. Classy but never fussy.
when_to_use: Use for sophisticated, cozy apartments with a 1960s New York feel. Leans dark and warm, so it suits evening scenes.
prompt_example: "library with brown lacquered walls and brass bookshelves, Billy Baldwin style, lamplight"

name: Sister Parish
definition: American decorator (1910-1994) famous for the cozy American country look: patchwork quilts, painted floors, knitted throws, chintz and baskets.
when_to_use: Use for warm, lived-in country rooms with a homemade touch. Pairs well with quilts and soft daylight.
prompt_example: "bedroom with patchwork quilt and painted floor, Sister Parish style"

name: David Hicks
definition: English designer (1929-1998) known for bold geometric carpets, hexagon patterns and daring color clashes like hot pink with orange.
when_to_use: Use for punchy 1960s and 70s rooms full of graphic pattern. Great for color, not for calm.
prompt_example: "living room with hexagon patterned carpet, pink and orange, David Hicks style"

name: Jean-Michel Frank
definition: French designer (1895-1941) who made quiet luxury: plain rooms in cream and beige, walls of parchment or straw, and chunky simple chairs and tables.
when_to_use: Use for soft, minimal, very rich-looking rooms. The magic is in the textures, so name materials like parchment, straw or leather.
prompt_example: "cream salon with parchment walls and block armchairs, Jean-Michel Frank style"

name: Syrie Maugham
definition: English decorator (1879-1955) famous for her all-white room: white walls, white satin, white flowers and mirrored screens, all glowing together.
when_to_use: Use for bright, dreamy, all-white spaces with a 1930s elegance. Add one soft accent if the image feels washed out.
prompt_example: "all-white drawing room, mirrored screen, white lilies, Syrie Maugham style"

name: Florence Knoll
definition: American architect and designer (1917-2019) who shaped the tidy mid-century office: open plans, low sleek sofas, slim steel legs, neat grids and calm blocks of color.
when_to_use: Use for clean, organized 1950s offices and modern lounges. Feels polished rather than cozy.
prompt_example: "1950s executive office, low sleek sofa, walnut desk, Florence Knoll style"
pairs_well_with: mid-century modern;ludwig mies van der rohe;teal and orange

name: Chesterfield Sofa
definition: A deep-buttoned leather sofa with rolled arms the same height as the back. Classic gentleman's club furniture.
when_to_use: Use for libraries, studies and cozy old-world rooms. Brown leather is the classic, but velvet versions look great too.
prompt_example: "oxblood leather Chesterfield sofa in a wood-paneled study, lamplight"

name: Egg Chair
definition: A curved, swiveling lounge chair shaped like a hollow egg with the front scooped out, so you sit tucked inside it.
when_to_use: Use for retro modern lounges, hotel lobbies and sci-fi homes. A fun single hero piece.
prompt_example: "bright red egg chair in a white lobby, soft daylight"

name: Shaker Furniture
definition: Plain, beautifully made wooden furniture from an American religious community: ladderback chairs, peg rails and simple cabinets with no decoration.
when_to_use: Use for calm, honest, handmade rooms. Very quiet, so pair it with soft daylight.
prompt_example: "Shaker ladderback chairs and peg rail, plain wooden room, window light"

name: Rattan Peacock Chair
definition: A woven wicker chair with a giant fan-shaped back that frames whoever sits in it like a throne.
when_to_use: Use for boho portraits, 1970s glamour and tropical porches. Instantly makes a seated person the star.
prompt_example: "woman in a white dress seated in a rattan peacock chair, tropical porch"

name: Louis XV Armchair
definition: An 18th century French armchair with curvy cabriole legs, carved gilded wood and soft padded silk seats.
when_to_use: Use for palace rooms, fancy portraits and romantic period scenes. Pairs with pastel silks and gold.
prompt_example: "gilded Louis XV armchair in pale blue silk, palace salon"

name: Tufted Ottoman
definition: A low padded footstool or bench with buttons pressed into the cushion, making a pattern of soft puffs.
when_to_use: Use as a cozy, luxurious detail in living rooms and dressing rooms. Small, so it works best as part of a scene.
prompt_example: "blush velvet tufted ottoman at the foot of a bed, soft morning light"

name: Windsor Chair
definition: A classic wooden chair with a solid carved seat and a back made of many thin spindles, often in a hoop shape.
when_to_use: Use for farmhouse kitchens, old taverns and cozy cottages. Feels old-fashioned in the best way.
prompt_example: "Windsor chairs around a scrubbed pine table, cottage kitchen"

name: Chaise Longue
definition: A long upholstered chair you can stretch your legs out on, with one raised end like a half sofa.
when_to_use: Use for lazy, elegant lounging scenes and dreamy portraits. Great for a reclining pose.
prompt_example: "woman reading on a velvet chaise longue by a tall window"

name: Raku
definition: Pottery pulled red hot from the kiln, leaving smoky black cracks, crackled white glaze and flashes of copper and rainbow sheen.
when_to_use: Use for earthy, dramatic pots with a lucky, unpredictable look. Every piece looks one of a kind.
prompt_example: "raku vase with copper flashes and smoky crackle, dark background"

name: Celadon
definition: A soft jade-green glaze, glassy and pale, used on Chinese and Korean pottery for over a thousand years.
when_to_use: Use for serene, elegant pottery and calm still lifes. The green is gentle, so avoid busy colors around it.
prompt_example: "celadon tea bowl on a linen cloth, soft window light"

name: Kintsugi
definition: The Japanese art of mending broken pottery with gold, so the cracks become shining golden rivers across the piece.
when_to_use: Use for healing, beauty in flaws and quiet luxury. Works as a metaphor too, like gold seams on a face or a heart.
prompt_example: "black kintsugi bowl with gold seams, dark slate, single soft light"

name: Delftware
definition: Glossy white Dutch pottery painted in soft cobalt blue: windmills, tulips, ships and little country scenes.
when_to_use: Use for charming tabletop scenes, tile patterns and cozy Dutch kitchens. Close cousin of blue and white porcelain, but more folksy and storybook.
prompt_example: "stack of delftware plates and a tulip vase on a sunny windowsill"

name: Majolica
definition: Glossy pottery with a milky white glaze painted in bright yellows, blues, greens and oranges, often with flowers, fruit and swirls.
when_to_use: Use for cheerful painted plates, jugs and tiles with an Italian or Spanish feel. Busy patterns, so keep the setting simple.
prompt_example: "majolica plates with lemons and blue swirls on a white wall"

name: Blue and White Porcelain
definition: Smooth white porcelain painted with cobalt blue dragons, flowers and landscapes. First perfected in China and loved worldwide.
when_to_use: Use for elegant vases, tea sets and patterned backgrounds. One of the most recognizable ceramic looks there is.
prompt_example: "blue and white porcelain ginger jar with peonies, soft studio light"

name: Speckled Stoneware
definition: Sturdy handmade mugs and plates in creamy or oatmeal glaze dotted with tiny brown speckles, like a bird egg.
when_to_use: Use for cozy cafe tables and modern handmade kitchen scenes. Feels homey and current.
prompt_example: "speckled stoneware mug of coffee on a wooden table, morning light"

name: Wood-Fired Pottery
definition: Pots baked for days in a wood-burning kiln, so flying ash melts into drippy glaze and flame marks paint warm browns, oranges and greens.
when_to_use: Use for rustic, natural pottery that looks touched by fire. Every surface is uneven, which is the charm.
prompt_example: "wood-fired jar with ash glaze drips, stone shelf, warm side light"

name: Linocut
definition: A print carved into a block of lino, so you get bold chunky shapes, white gouge marks and solid flat ink.
when_to_use: Use for punchy posters, folk-style animals and bold book illustrations. Not for fine soft detail.
prompt_example: "linocut print of a fox in the snow, black ink on cream paper"

name: Screen Print
definition: Flat, bold layers of ink pushed through a mesh screen. Bright solid colors, slightly off-register edges, like gig posters and pop art.
when_to_use: Use for poppy posters, t-shirt graphics and bold portraits. Limit to a few colors for the most believable look.
prompt_example: "screen print poster of a surfer, three colors, slightly misaligned"

name: Risograph
definition: A grainy stencil printing look with bright see-through inks like fluoro pink and teal that overlap into new colors.
when_to_use: Use for zines, indie posters and playful illustrations with a soft, grainy texture. Fine detail can blur.
prompt_example: "risograph print of a cat in a plant shop, pink and teal ink"

name: Cyanotype
definition: A sun print in deep Prussian blue, where objects laid on special paper leave crisp white ghostly shapes.
when_to_use: Use for botanical prints, dreamy photos and vintage science looks. Everything turns blue and white, so plan for that.
prompt_example: "cyanotype of fern leaves and wildflowers, deep blue and white"

name: Letterpress
definition: Old-school printing with metal or wood type pressed into thick paper, so letters sit in a slight dent with rich, slightly uneven ink.
