when_to_use: Use for invitations, posters and type that looks touchable. AI can still misspell words, so keep text short.
prompt_example: "letterpress wedding invitation, cotton paper, deep debossed letters"

name: Monotype
definition: A one-off print made by painting on a smooth plate and pressing paper onto it, giving soft, smudgy, painterly marks.
when_to_use: Use for moody, loose, one-of-a-kind art prints. Expect a dreamy, imperfect finish, not crisp lines.
prompt_example: "monotype print of a figure by the sea, smudgy gray and blue ink"

name: Woodblock Print
definition: Pictures printed from carved wooden blocks, one block per color, with flat areas of color and wood grain sometimes showing through.
when_to_use: Use for Japanese-style landscapes, waves and gentle folk scenes. Pairs well with soft natural colors.
prompt_example: "woodblock print of a mountain village in snow, indigo and red"

name: Etching
definition: A print made from lines scratched into a metal plate and bitten with acid, so the picture is built from fine crosshatched lines.
when_to_use: Use for old book illustrations, maps and detailed vintage scenes. Mostly black and white, with tiny delicate lines.
prompt_example: "etching of an old harbor town, fine crosshatching, sepia ink"

name: Embroidery
definition: Pictures and patterns stitched with colored thread onto fabric, with raised, glossy stitches you can almost feel.
when_to_use: Use for cozy, handmade looks on clothes, hoops and patches. Great for flowers, animals and lettering.
prompt_example: "embroidery hoop with wildflowers and a bee, linen fabric, close-up"

name: Macrame
definition: Thick cotton cord knotted by hand into wall hangings, plant hangers and fringes with lots of soft texture.
when_to_use: Use for boho rooms, 1970s vibes and natural, handmade decor. Usually cream or natural colors.
prompt_example: "macrame wall hanging above a bed, trailing plants, morning sun"

name: Quilting
definition: Blankets sewn from many fabric patches into patterns like stars, squares and zigzags, with soft puffy stitching.
when_to_use: Use for homey, nostalgic, warm scenes and colorful patterns. Also great as a style, like a quilted landscape.
prompt_example: "patchwork quilt of red and blue stars on a porch rocking chair"

name: Mosaic
definition: Pictures made from hundreds of tiny tiles, glass or broken pottery pieces set side by side, with thin lines of grout between them.
when_to_use: Use for floors, walls, fountains and ancient or playful murals. Faces can get blocky, which is part of the charm.
prompt_example: "mosaic of a peacock made from broken colorful tiles, sunlit wall"

name: Marquetry
definition: Pictures made by fitting thin slices of different colored woods together like a jigsaw on furniture or panels.
when_to_use: Use for elegant antique furniture and warm, detailed wooden artwork. Works best in close-ups.
prompt_example: "marquetry tabletop with flowers in inlaid woods, warm light"

name: Beadwork
definition: Designs made from tiny glass beads sewn or strung together, sparkling in bright rows and patterns.
when_to_use: Use for jewelry, bags, clothing details and bright patterned art. Many cultures have their own beadwork traditions, so name one if you can.
prompt_example: "beadwork pouch with a floral pattern, colorful glass beads, close-up"

name: Weaving
definition: Threads crossed over and under on a loom to make cloth, rugs and wall hangings, with visible texture and stripes.
when_to_use: Use for cozy textiles, handmade rugs and textured art pieces. Name colors and patterns to guide it.
prompt_example: "handwoven wall tapestry in rust and cream stripes, loom in the corner"

name: Needlepoint
definition: Tiny even stitches of wool worked across a stiff canvas grid, filling every space to make a soft, pixel-like picture.
when_to_use: Use for cushions, vintage samplers and cozy grandma-chic decor. The grid gives a slightly blocky look.
prompt_example: "needlepoint cushion with a pug and roses, wool stitches, armchair"

name: Knitting
definition: Soft loops of yarn growing off two needles, often with a ball of wool rolling nearby. Chunky stitches read as warmth you can almost feel.
when_to_use: Use for cozy winter scenes, slow-living moments, or a gentle hands-at-work shot. Close crops work best, since fine stitches can turn to mush in wide shots.
prompt_example: "knitting a chunky cream scarf by the window, rainy afternoon"

name: Scrapbooking
definition: Pages layered with photos, washi tape, ticket stubs, pressed flowers and handwritten notes. A happy, collected mess of memories.
when_to_use: Use for nostalgic flat lays, journaling vibes, or a memory-board look. Any written words may come out garbled, so keep the text small or skip it.
prompt_example: "scrapbook page with polaroids, washi tape and pressed flowers, flat lay"

name: Model Train Layout
definition: A tiny world on a tabletop: miniature trains winding past little towns, tunnels, trees and lakes. Everything looks small, careful and loved.
when_to_use: Use for charming miniature scenes or a nostalgic hobby room. Add macro photography to sell the tiny scale.
prompt_example: "model train layout with a snowy mountain village, warm lamp light"

name: Bonsai
definition: A tree kept small in a shallow pot, trimmed and shaped to look old and windswept. Quiet, patient and full of character.
when_to_use: Use for calm, minimal scenes and Japanese-inspired still lifes. It shines on a plain background where its shape can breathe.
prompt_example: "twisted juniper bonsai on a wooden stand, soft morning light"

name: Terrarium
definition: A tiny garden sealed inside glass: moss, ferns, pebbles and sometimes a little figurine. A whole world you can hold in your hands.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy miniature worlds and cozy shelf scenes. Glass reflections can get busy, so a dark or plain background helps.
prompt_example: "glass terrarium with moss, tiny ferns and a sleeping fox figurine"

name: Candle Making
definition: Melted wax being poured into jars, with wicks held straight and dried flowers on the side. Warm, homey and a little bit magical.
when_to_use: Use for cozy workshop scenes and slow, satisfying pouring shots. It works for video too, as a gentle pour.
prompt_example: "pouring cream wax into amber jars, dried lavender on the table"

name: Cross-Stitch
definition: Tiny X-shaped stitches on a grid of fabric, held tight in a wooden hoop. Pictures made one little square at a time.
when_to_use: Use for folk patterns, cute samplers and homey craft scenes. Stitched letters rarely come out right, so lean on flowers and shapes.
prompt_example: "cross-stitch of wildflowers in a wooden hoop, embroidery floss scattered around"

name: Pottery Wheel
definition: Wet clay spinning under muddy hands as a bowl rises from the middle. Earthy, slow and very satisfying to watch.
when_to_use: Use for calm studio scenes and hands-at-work close-ups. A great pick for video, where the spinning clay really comes alive.
prompt_example: "hands shaping a clay bowl on a spinning pottery wheel, dusty studio light"

name: Charcuterie Board
definition: A wooden board piled with cured meats, cheeses, grapes, crackers, nuts and honey. Generous, colorful and made for sharing.
when_to_use: Use for party spreads, cozy gatherings and overhead food shots. It looks best from straight above.
prompt_example: "charcuterie board with figs, brie and honeycomb, overhead shot"

name: Ramen Bowl
definition: A deep bowl of noodles in rich broth, topped with a soft egg, green onions and sliced pork. Warm and comforting in one look.
when_to_use: Use for cozy night-in scenes or late-night street food moods. Add steam rising to make it feel hot and fresh.
prompt_example: "ramen bowl, soft-boiled egg, steam rising, dark wooden counter"
pairs_well_with: steam rising;neon glow;shallow depth of field

name: Layered Trifle
definition: A tall glass bowl showing neat stripes of sponge cake, custard, fruit and whipped cream. Pretty from the side, like a dessert cross-section.
when_to_use: Use for celebration tables and vintage-style dessert shots. Shoot from the side so the layers show.
prompt_example: "layered trifle with raspberries and cream in a glass bowl, side view"

name: Street Tacos
definition: Small corn tortillas loaded with grilled meat, onion, cilantro and a squeeze of lime. Bright, messy and full of life.
when_to_use: Use for lively street food scenes and colorful, casual food shots. A paper plate or food truck backdrop keeps it real.
prompt_example: "three street tacos with lime wedges on a paper plate, food truck at dusk"

name: Macarons
definition: Small round almond cookies with smooth shells, frilly edges and a creamy filling. They come in every soft color you can imagine.
when_to_use: Use for cute, pastel dessert scenes and tea party tables. Stack them or line them up for a neat, pretty pattern.
prompt_example: "stack of pastel macarons on a marble table, soft window light"

name: Dim Sum
definition: Little dumplings and buns tucked into round bamboo steamer baskets, often with tea on the side. Delicate, shiny and inviting.
when_to_use: Use for warm family table scenes and close-up dumpling shots. Pair with steam rising so the baskets feel fresh.
prompt_example: "bamboo steamer baskets of dim sum dumplings, steam rising, teapot nearby"

name: Wood-Fired Pizza
definition: A round pizza with puffy, charred, blistered edges, fresh from a glowing brick oven. Bubbling cheese and a bit of basil on top.
when_to_use: Use for rustic kitchen scenes and warm, glowing food shots. The fire in the oven behind adds lovely warm light.
prompt_example: "wood-fired pizza on a peel, glowing brick oven behind, basil leaves"

name: Pancake Stack
definition: A tall, fluffy tower of pancakes with butter melting on top and syrup running down the sides. Breakfast at its happiest.
when_to_use: Use for cheerful morning scenes and indulgent food shots. Add syrup drizzle for that sticky, mouthwatering moment.
prompt_example: "tall pancake stack, melting butter, syrup drizzle, sunny kitchen"
pairs_well_with: syrup drizzle;golden hour;shallow depth of field

name: Steam Rising
definition: Soft wisps of steam curling up from hot food or drink. It tells the eye this is fresh and warm.
when_to_use: Use on soups, coffee, noodles and anything that should look hot. It shows up best against a dark background with light from the side or behind.
prompt_example: "cup of black coffee, steam rising, dark background, side light"

name: Cheese Pull
definition: Long, stretchy strings of melted cheese pulling apart as a slice or sandwich is lifted. Gooey and impossible to ignore.
when_to_use: Use for pizza, grilled cheese and lasagna shots that need instant appetite. Strings can come out looking like rubber, so add words like melted and gooey.
prompt_example: "lifting a slice of pizza, long cheese pull, warm light"

name: Syrup Drizzle
definition: A thin, glossy ribbon of syrup or honey flowing down onto food. It catches the light like liquid amber.
when_to_use: Use on pancakes, waffles and desserts for a sticky, sweet moment. Backlight makes the drizzle glow.
prompt_example: "honey drizzle onto a stack of waffles, backlit, golden light"

name: Sizzle
definition: Food hitting a hot pan or grill with popping oil, little bursts of smoke and browning edges. You can almost hear it.
when_to_use: Use for cooking action, grills and street food scenes. It works best in video, where the bubbling oil can move.
prompt_example: "steak sizzling in a cast iron pan, oil spatter, smoky kitchen light"

name: Flour Dust
definition: A soft cloud of flour puffing up from hands, dough or a counter. Floating specks catch the light like snow.
when_to_use: Use for baking scenes and homey kitchen moments. A beam of side light makes the dust glow.
prompt_example: "baker clapping floured hands, flour dust in a sunbeam, rustic kitchen"

name: Glossy Glaze
definition: A shiny, mirror-like coating on food, like a donut glaze, a caramel layer or a sticky roast. It gleams with highlights.
when_to_use: Use when food needs to look rich, fresh and expensive. Too much shine can look plastic, so pair it with natural light.
prompt_example: "mirror glaze cake with glossy berry topping, soft window light"

name: Splash Shot
definition: A drink or fruit frozen mid-splash, with droplets and liquid crowns flying in the air. Fresh, bold and full of energy.
when_to_use: Use for drinks, fruit and juicy, refreshing ads. Pair with slow motion for video, or a frozen moment for stills.
prompt_example: "strawberry dropping into milk, splash shot, white background"

name: Condensation Droplets
definition: Tiny beads of water clinging to the outside of a cold glass or bottle. They make a drink look ice-cold and refreshing.
when_to_use: Use for cold drinks, iced coffee and summer scenes. Close shots with backlight make the droplets sparkle.
prompt_example: "iced lemonade glass covered in condensation droplets, sunny patio"

name: Jazz Club
definition: A dim, smoky room with a small stage, a glowing saxophone, round tables and warm lamps. Late-night and full of soul.
when_to_use: Use for moody night scenes, vintage glamour and cozy after-hours stories. It loves warm light and deep shadows.
prompt_example: "jazz club stage, saxophone player in a spotlight, smoky air, warm lamps"

name: Vinyl Record
definition: A black disc with fine grooves spinning on a turntable, the needle resting gently on top. Warm, analog and nostalgic.
when_to_use: Use for retro music moods, cozy listening corners and close-up texture shots. Spinning works nicely in video too.
prompt_example: "vinyl record spinning on a turntable, warm lamp light, record sleeves behind"

name: Concert Stage Lights
definition: Bright beams of colored light cutting through haze above a stage and a crowd. Big, loud energy you can see.
when_to_use: Use for gigs, festivals and big hero moments. Haze or fog is what makes the beams show, so add it in.
prompt_example: "rock band on stage, colored concert stage lights through haze, crowd silhouettes"

name: Synthwave
definition: A retro-future look from 80s electronic music: neon pinks and purples, glowing grid floors, chrome text and a striped setting sun.
when_to_use: Use for retro night drives, neon cityscapes and album-cover vibes. It is a strong look, so it can take over the whole image.
prompt_example: "synthwave sunset, neon grid road, palm silhouettes, purple sky"

name: Orchestra Pit
definition: A sunken space in front of a theater stage, packed with musicians, music stands and little lamps. Elegant and a bit hidden.
when_to_use: Use for grand theater nights and classical music scenes. Shoot from above to show the rows of players.
prompt_example: "orchestra pit from above, small stand lamps, velvet theater seats"

name: Lo-Fi Bedroom Studio
definition: A small, messy bedroom with a keyboard, headphones, a laptop, plants and fairy lights. Chill, homemade music vibes.
when_to_use: Use for study and chill moods, cozy illustrations and late-night creative scenes. It looks lovely as an anime-style drawing too.
prompt_example: "lo-fi bedroom studio at night, keyboard and headphones, fairy lights, rain on the window"

name: Sheet Music
definition: Pages of musical notes on lined staffs, often aged and curling at the edges. Romantic and a little old-world.
when_to_use: Use for vintage still lifes, romantic scenes and paper-texture backgrounds. The notes will not be real music, so do not count on readable melodies.
prompt_example: "old sheet music on a piano, dried roses, candlelight"

name: Cassette Tape
definition: A small plastic tape case with two little reels and a handwritten label. Pure mixtape nostalgia.
when_to_use: Use for retro, 80s and 90s scenes, flat lays and nostalgic music moments. Handwritten labels may come out scrambled.
prompt_example: "cassette tape with a handwritten label on a desk, retro colors, flat lay"

name: Ballet Arabesque
definition: A ballerina balanced on one leg with the other stretched straight out behind her, arms reaching long. Graceful and still.
when_to_use: Use for elegant, poised moments and soft stage scenes. Bodies can bend oddly, so keep the pose simple and the dancer in full view.
prompt_example: "ballerina in an arabesque, pale tutu, soft stage light, dark background"

name: Flamenco
definition: A fiery Spanish dance with swirling ruffled skirts, stamping heels, proud posture and sharp hand movements. Passion in motion.
when_to_use: Use for dramatic, colorful scenes with lots of movement and feeling. The flying skirt looks amazing in video.
prompt_example: "flamenco dancer in a red ruffled dress, skirt mid-swirl, warm spotlight"

name: Breakdancing Freeze
definition: A breakdancer stopped mid-move, balanced on one hand or their head with legs locked in the air. Bold, strong and surprising.
when_to_use: Use for street culture, high-energy scenes and urban portraits. Balances can look awkward, so a low angle helps sell the power.
prompt_example: "breakdancer in a freeze on one hand, city street at night, low angle"

name: Ballroom Waltz
definition: A couple gliding across a polished floor in a gentle three-step turn, gown flowing out behind. Old-fashioned romance.
when_to_use: Use for elegant, romantic scenes and grand ballroom moments. Chandeliers and a soft glow complete the feeling.
prompt_example: "couple in a ballroom waltz, flowing gown, crystal chandeliers, warm glow"

name: Contemporary Dance
definition: Free, flowing movement that mixes reaching, falling and rolling, often barefoot in simple clothes. Expressive and emotional.
when_to_use: Use for feelings that are hard to say: grief, joy, longing. Keep backgrounds simple so the body tells the story.
prompt_example: "contemporary dancer mid-leap, loose white clothes, empty studio, window light"

name: Tap Dance
definition: Quick, rhythmic footwork in shoes with metal plates on the soles, clicking on a wooden floor. Bright, bouncy showmanship.
when_to_use: Use for playful, old-time stage vibes and fun footwork close-ups. The sound is the point, so pick it for video with audio when you can.
prompt_example: "close-up of tap shoes on a wooden stage, spotlight, vintage theater"

name: Tango
definition: A close, intense partner dance with sharp turns, leg flicks and dramatic dips. Sultry and full of tension.
when_to_use: Use for passionate, moody scenes and evening romance. Pairs well with dim, warm light and deep shadows.
prompt_example: "couple dancing tango, dramatic dip, dim smoky room, warm light"

name: Swing Dance
definition: A joyful, bouncy partner dance with spins, kicks and lifts, straight out of old dance halls. Smiles and flying skirts.
when_to_use: Use for happy, vintage party scenes and big energy. Lifts and flips can tangle limbs, so keep it to spins and kicks.
prompt_example: "couple swing dancing, polka dot dress mid-spin, 1940s dance hall"

name: Fire
definition: Flickering orange and yellow flames that glow, dance and throw warm light on everything near them.
when_to_use: Use for warmth, danger or drama, from a cozy hearth to a wild blaze. It also works as a strong light source in dark scenes.
prompt_example: "campfire in a dark forest, flames lighting the faces around it"

name: Liquid Mercury
definition: A silvery liquid metal that beads up into perfect, mirror-like drops and pools. It reflects everything around it.
when_to_use: Use for futuristic, sleek, otherworldly looks. Mirror surfaces pick up their surroundings, so choose a simple scene.
prompt_example: "drops of liquid mercury on black glass, studio light, macro"

name: Crystal Formations
definition: Clusters of sharp, glassy crystals growing in points and facets, like inside a geode or a cave. Light sparkles through them.
when_to_use: Use for magical caves, gem close-ups and fantasy landscapes. Backlight makes them glow from inside.
prompt_example: "amethyst crystal formations inside a geode, glowing backlight"

name: Plasma
definition: Glowing, electric gas that crackles in branching purple and pink threads, like inside a plasma ball. Alive with energy.
when_to_use: Use for sci-fi power, magic spells and electric moods. Dark backgrounds make the glowing threads stand out.
prompt_example: "plasma ball with purple electric threads, dark room"

name: Northern Lights
definition: Ribbons of green, and sometimes pink and purple, light rippling across a dark polar sky. Nature's own light show.
when_to_use: Use for magical night landscapes and quiet wonder. Snowy ground and a still lake for reflections make it shine.
prompt_example: "northern lights over a snowy cabin, green ribbons reflected in a lake"

name: Cloud Chamber
definition: A dark, misty box where invisible particles from space leave thin, wispy trails that appear and fade, like tiny shooting stars.
when_to_use: Use for mysterious science scenes and abstract, starry textures. It is a niche idea, so describe the wispy trails in your prompt too.
prompt_example: "cloud chamber, thin glowing particle trails in mist, black background"

name: Ferrofluid
definition: A black, magnetic liquid that rises into spiky, hedgehog-like shapes when a magnet comes near. Strange, shiny and hypnotic.
when_to_use: Use for weird, futuristic close-ups and satisfying motion. It looks best in video, where the spikes grow and melt back.
prompt_example: "black ferrofluid forming spikes on a mirror, studio light, macro"

name: Soap Bubble
definition: A thin floating sphere that swirls with rainbow colors on its skin, catching tiny reflections of the world around it.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy, playful and magical moments, and close-ups full of color. Great slow-moving in video too.
prompt_example: "giant soap bubble drifting over a meadow, rainbow swirls, golden hour"

name: Sunflower
definition: Tall stems carrying big golden faces with dark centers, all turned toward the light. Happy, warm and summery.
when_to_use: Use for cheerful countryside scenes, portraits in a field and warm yellow palettes. Late afternoon sun makes the petals glow.
prompt_example: "girl in a straw hat in a sunflower field, late afternoon light"

name: Monstera
definition: A big, glossy houseplant with heart-shaped leaves full of splits and holes. Tropical, bold and very photogenic.
when_to_use: Use for jungle interiors, modern plant corners and leafy shadow patterns. Its leaf shape is easy for AI to get right.
prompt_example: "monstera plant in a sunny corner, leaf shadows on a white wall"

name: Ferns
definition: Soft, feathery fronds that curl open from little spirals, filling shady forest floors in layers of green.
when_to_use: Use for lush woodland scenes, fairy worlds and green, shady corners. They love misty, soft light.
prompt_example: "forest floor of ferns, morning mist, soft green light"

name: Wild Poppies
definition: Bright red, paper-thin petals with dark centers, nodding in tall grass. Delicate, cheerful and a little bit wild.
when_to_use: Use for summer meadows, nostalgic countryside and pops of red. They look lovely swaying in the wind on video.
prompt_example: "meadow of wild poppies swaying in the wind, golden hour"

name: Rosemary
definition: A woody herb with needle-like, silvery green leaves and tiny pale blue flowers. Rustic and fresh, like a cottage kitchen.
when_to_use: Use for herb gardens, rustic kitchen still lifes and cooking scenes. Small sprigs make a nice garnish detail in food shots.
prompt_example: "rosemary sprigs on a wooden board with sea salt and olive oil"

name: Wisteria
definition: Long, hanging clusters of purple or white flowers dripping from vines over arches and walls. Like a flower waterfall.
when_to_use: Use for fairytale gardens, romantic walkways and dreamy spring scenes. Light coming through the blooms adds magic.
prompt_example: "wisteria tunnel in full bloom, soft light through purple flowers"

name: Succulents
definition: Plump, fleshy little plants growing in neat rosettes, in shades of sage, blue-green and dusty pink.
when_to_use: Use for desert gardens, tidy windowsills and soft, pastel plant arrangements. They look great from above.
prompt_example: "arrangement of succulents in terracotta pots, overhead, soft light"

name: Eucalyptus
definition: Round, coin-shaped or long leaves in a soft silvery blue-green, often tied in loose bunches. Fresh and calm.
when_to_use: Use for wedding florals, spa-like scenes and gentle green palettes. A few sprigs soften almost any still life.
prompt_example: "bunch of eucalyptus in a glass vase, soft daylight, linen backdrop"

name: Copper Patina
definition: Copper that has turned a soft blue-green over time, with patches of warm brown still showing through. Old, weathered and beautiful.
when_to_use: Use for aged rooftops, antique objects and fantasy ruins. It adds history to anything it touches.
prompt_example: "old copper dome with green patina, cloudy sky"

name: Hammered Gold
definition: Gold covered in tiny dents and dimples from being shaped by hand. Each little dip catches the light and sparkles.
when_to_use: Use for luxury jewelry, rich tableware and opulent details. It looks warmer and more handmade than smooth gold.
prompt_example: "hammered gold bowl on black velvet, soft spotlight"

name: Oxidized Iron
definition: Iron eaten by rust into flaky orange, brown and red layers. Rough, gritty and full of age.
when_to_use: Use for abandoned places, industrial textures and gritty moods. It pairs well with grey skies and decay.
prompt_example: "rusty oxidized iron gate, peeling texture, overcast day"

name: Chrome
definition: Super shiny, mirror-like silver metal that reflects everything around it in curved, warped shapes.
when_to_use: Use for retro cars, futuristic designs and bold, glossy objects. Reflections can get messy, so a clean setting helps.
prompt_example: "chrome sphere on a checkered floor reflecting neon lights"

name: Pewter
definition: A soft, dull grey metal with a gentle, low shine, often seen in old mugs, plates and candlesticks. Quiet and old-world.
when_to_use: Use for medieval feasts, rustic tables and muted still lifes. It is less flashy than silver, which is the point.
prompt_example: "pewter tankards and candlesticks on a rough wooden table"

name: Brass
definition: A warm, golden-yellow metal that shines softly and darkens with age. Think old instruments, lamps and door knobs.
when_to_use: Use for vintage interiors, steampunk details and cozy warm glow. It is warmer and more lived-in than gold.
prompt_example: "old brass telescope on a desk, warm lamp light, maps behind"

name: Gunmetal
definition: A dark blue-gray metal with a soft satin shine. Serious, sleek and a little moody.
when_to_use: Use for tech products, watches, sci-fi gear and modern interiors. It reads darker than chrome, so add a light to bring out the edges.
prompt_example: "gunmetal wristwatch on black slate, single soft side light"

name: Damascus Steel
definition: Steel with flowing, wavy light and dark patterns rippling across it, like wood grain or water. Each blade is one of a kind.
when_to_use: Use for knives, swords and close-up texture shots. The pattern is the star, so get close.
prompt_example: "close-up of a damascus steel blade with wavy patterns, dark background"

name: Snow Leopard
definition: A big wild cat with smoky gray fur, dark rosettes, pale eyes and a huge fluffy tail. It looks like winter itself turned into an animal.
when_to_use: Use for icy mountain scenes and quiet, powerful portraits. Say snow leopard in full, or you may get a regular leopard standing in snow.
prompt_example: "snow leopard resting on a snowy rock ledge, first snow, soft light"

name: Axolotl
definition: A smiling pink salamander with feathery frills around its head, like a little underwater dragon. Soft, glossy and a bit unreal.
when_to_use: Use for cute creatures, aquarium scenes and dreamy fantasy pets. Models sometimes add extra legs or frills, so check the details.
prompt_example: "pink axolotl in a glowing aquarium, macro photography"

name: Peacock
definition: A bird with a giant fan of green and blue tail feathers, each one marked with a shimmering eye. Pure color and showing off.
when_to_use: Use when you want jewel colors and drama in one word. Ask for tail fanned out if you want the full display.
prompt_example: "peacock with tail fanned out in a palace garden, jewel tones"

name: Koi
definition: Big ornamental carp in white, orange, red and black, gliding through clear pond water. Calm, lucky and very Japanese garden.
when_to_use: Use for peaceful pond scenes and swirling patterns of fish. They look best seen from above through clear water.
prompt_example: "koi swimming in a clear pond under floating maple leaves, top-down view"

name: Red Fox
definition: A slim fox with flame-orange fur, a white chest, black socks and a bushy tail. Clever, alert and gorgeous against snow or autumn leaves.
when_to_use: Use for storybook woodland scenes and wildlife portraits. It pops most against cool blue or green backgrounds.
prompt_example: "red fox in a frosty meadow at sunrise, golden hour"

name: Highland Cow
definition: A shaggy Scottish cow with long ginger hair over its eyes and wide curved horns. Scruffy, gentle and wildly lovable.
when_to_use: Use for cozy countryside scenes, cute farm portraits and misty hills. The fringe over the eyes is the charm, so keep the face close.
prompt_example: "highland cow in misty Scottish hills, fog, overcast light"

name: Jellyfish
definition: Soft, see-through bells trailing long ribbon tentacles, drifting like living lanterns. In the dark they can glow.
when_to_use: Use for calm underwater scenes, dreamy floating shapes and glowing night images. Lovely in video because they move so slowly.
prompt_example: "jellyfish drifting in dark water, bioluminescence, ethereal"

name: Barn Owl
definition: A pale owl with a white heart-shaped face, dark eyes and soft gold and gray wings. It looks like a friendly ghost at dusk.
when_to_use: Use for gentle spooky night scenes, old barns and fairy tale moods. Say barn owl to get the heart-shaped face.
prompt_example: "barn owl in flight over a meadow at dusk, rim light"

name: Ansel Adams
definition: (1902-1984) American landscape photographer famous for huge black and white views of mountains, lakes and Yosemite. Deep blacks, bright whites and every gray in between.
when_to_use: Use for grand, crisp black and white nature scenes. He shot landscapes, so it helps less with people or color.
prompt_example: "misty mountain lake, in the style of Ansel Adams, black and white"

name: Dorothea Lange
definition: (1895-1965) American documentary photographer known for honest, tender portraits of working families during the Great Depression. Plain black and white, weathered faces, quiet strength.
when_to_use: Use for serious, human portraits with an old American feel. The style is about dignity, not drama, so keep subjects respectful.
prompt_example: "farm worker resting by a truck, 1930s, in the style of Dorothea Lange"

name: Vivian Maier
definition: (1926-2009) American street photographer who secretly took well over 100,000 photos while working as a nanny. Square black and white street moments and clever self-portraits in shop windows.
when_to_use: Use for mid-century city street scenes and reflection self-portraits. Set it in the 1950s or 1960s for the real flavor.
prompt_example: "woman's reflection in a shop window, 1950s Chicago street, in the style of Vivian Maier"

name: Richard Avedon
definition: (1923-2004) American fashion and portrait photographer known for people posed against plain white backgrounds. Sharp, direct and full of energy and personality.
when_to_use: Use for bold fashion portraits and striking faces on clean white. Not the right pick for moody or misty scenes.
prompt_example: "model mid-leap on a white backdrop, in the style of Richard Avedon, black and white"

name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
definition: (1908-2004) French photographer who mastered the decisive moment, the split second when everything in a street scene lines up just right. Black and white, natural and beautifully balanced.
when_to_use: Use for candid street scenes with perfect timing and shape. Works best with simple everyday action, like someone jumping a puddle.
prompt_example: "man leaping over a puddle in a Paris street, in the style of Henri Cartier-Bresson"

name: Saul Leiter
definition: (1923-2013) American photographer who shot New York in soft, painterly color. Think red umbrellas in snow, blurry shapes through fogged windows and shy little pops of color.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy, rainy, colorful city moments with lots of layers. If you want sharp and clear, pick someone else.
prompt_example: "red umbrella in falling snow seen through a steamy cafe window, in the style of Saul Leiter"

name: Irving Penn
definition: (1917-2009) American photographer known for elegant fashion portraits and still lifes against plain gray backdrops. Calm, precise and beautifully lit, like a museum piece.
when_to_use: Use for clean studio portraits, fashion and simple, perfect still lifes. It is a studio look, so it will not help outdoor scenes.
prompt_example: "still life of ripe pears on a gray backdrop, in the style of Irving Penn"

name: Gordon Parks
definition: (1912-2006) American photographer, filmmaker and writer who captured Black American life and the civil rights era for Life magazine. Warm, dignified portraits in rich color and black and white.
when_to_use: Use for heartfelt mid-century portraits and everyday family scenes with real warmth. Keep the people at the center and treat them with respect.
prompt_example: "family on a porch in 1950s Alabama, warm color, in the style of Gordon Parks"

name: Polaroid
definition: An instant photo with a thick white border and soft, slightly faded colors. Creamy highlights, gentle blur and a real snapshot feeling.
when_to_use: Use for nostalgic, personal, party or road trip images. Say Polaroid photo with white frame if you want the border to show.
prompt_example: "Polaroid photo of friends at a beach bonfire, white frame"

name: Kodachrome
definition: A famous old color slide film with rich reds, deep blues and warm, glowing skin. Think 1950s and 60s holiday slides.
when_to_use: Use for vivid, warm, mid-century color that feels real but extra beautiful. It pushes color hard, so keep the scene simple.
prompt_example: "Kodachrome photo of a 1960s roadside diner at noon"

name: Tintype
definition: An old portrait printed straight onto a thin metal plate, popular in the 1860s. Dark silvery tones, soft edges and serious faces staring right at you.
when_to_use: Use for haunting old-time portraits and Western or Victorian characters. Expect a dark, moody result, not a cheerful one.
prompt_example: "tintype portrait of a cowboy, 1860s, scratched plate edges"

name: Daguerreotype
definition: The very first popular kind of photograph, from 1839, made on a polished silver mirror. Ghostly, silvery, finely detailed images with a soft glow and dark edges.
when_to_use: Use for eerie, delicate, museum-like antique portraits. People sat very still for these, so keep poses calm.
prompt_example: "daguerreotype portrait of a young woman in a lace collar"

name: Disposable Camera
definition: The look of a cheap throwaway film camera: bright on-camera flash, red eyes, slight blur and grainy colors. Messy, fun and very real.
when_to_use: Use for party shots, teen memories and casual 90s or Y2K snapshots. It is meant to look imperfect, so do not expect polish.
prompt_example: "disposable camera photo of friends in a kitchen at night, flash"

name: Infrared Film
definition: Film that sees invisible light, turning green leaves and grass bright white or candy pink while skies go dark. Familiar places suddenly look like another planet.
when_to_use: Use for surreal landscapes and dreamy, otherworldly nature. Say black and white infrared for white trees, or color infrared for pink trees.
prompt_example: "color infrared photo of a forest lake, pink trees"

name: Lomography
definition: Photos from cheap toy cameras with heavy dark corners, oversaturated colors and happy little mistakes. Bold, blurry, punchy and full of character.
when_to_use: Use for playful, arty snapshots with loud color. If you want clean and sharp, this is the wrong word.
prompt_example: "lomography photo of a summer funfair, heavy vignette, saturated colors"

name: Pinhole Camera
definition: A tiny hole instead of a lens, giving soft, dreamy pictures with dark edges and everything gently in focus.
when_to_use: Use for quiet, timeless and slightly ghostly images. Nothing is sharp, so it is not the choice for crisp detail.
prompt_example: "pinhole camera photo of an old pier at dawn, soft vignette"

name: Light Painting
definition: Drawing with a moving light in the dark while the camera shutter stays open. You get glowing ribbons, swirls and shapes hanging in the air.
when_to_use: Use for night scenes with trails of light, sparkler hearts and glowing loops around people. Words written in light often come out misspelled.
prompt_example: "person drawing glowing spirals with a flashlight on a dark beach, light painting"

name: Prism Effect
definition: Holding a glass prism in front of the lens to throw rainbows, ghostly double edges and soft color streaks across the picture.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy portraits and music photos with a touch of magic. Too much can hide the face, so ask for rainbows at the edge of the frame.
prompt_example: "portrait with prism effect, rainbow light streaks along the edge of the frame"

name: Freelensing
definition: Taking the lens off the camera and holding it loosely in front. Only a thin slice stays sharp, and the rest melts into blur and glowing haze.
when_to_use: Use for soft, romantic portraits and flowers. It is unpredictable on purpose, so try a few versions.
prompt_example: "freelensing portrait of a bride in a meadow, thin slice of focus, hazy light"
pairs_well_with: shallow depth of field;light leak;golden hour

name: Intentional Camera Movement
definition: Moving the camera on purpose while the photo is taken, so trees, lights or the sea smear into painterly streaks.
when_to_use: Use for abstract, painterly nature and city images. Nothing will be sharp, and that is the point.
prompt_example: "intentional camera movement photo of a birch forest, vertical streaks"

name: Multiple Exposure
definition: Several pictures layered into one frame, so faces, cities and nature blend together like a memory.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy, emotional, story-filled images. Keep each layer simple, or the result turns into a busy jumble.
prompt_example: "multiple exposure of a woman's profile, a pine forest and a city skyline"

name: Smoke Bomb
definition: A burst of thick colored smoke filling the air around a subject. Pink, orange or teal clouds that swirl and glow in the light.
when_to_use: Use for bold fashion, wedding and music shots with big color. Pick one or two smoke colors for the cleanest look.
prompt_example: "dancer in a field with pink smoke bomb, backlit, golden hour"

name: Zoom Burst
definition: Zooming the lens while the photo is taken, so streaks shoot out from the center like you are flying forward.
when_to_use: Use for energy, speed and excitement, like a city at night rushing at you. The center stays clearest, so put your subject there.
prompt_example: "zoom burst photo of busy street lights at night"

name: Lensball
definition: A clear glass ball held up in front of a scene, showing a tiny upside-down copy of the world inside while the background blurs.
when_to_use: Use for magical travel shots, sunsets and landscapes with a twist. Remember the view inside the ball is flipped.
prompt_example: "lensball held up at sunset over a mountain lake, background bokeh"

name: Worm's-Eye View
definition: The view from the very ground looking straight up, as if you were a worm. Trees, buildings and people tower over you.
when_to_use: Use to make anything look huge, heroic or dizzying. It is more extreme than a plain low angle.
prompt_example: "worm's-eye view of skyscrapers and a lone tree, blue sky"

name: Through the Leaves
definition: The photo is taken from behind blurry leaves or flowers close to the lens, so the subject peeks out from soft green shapes.
when_to_use: Use for candid, hidden-observer moments and lush nature portraits. Ask for the leaves out of focus so they frame instead of block.
prompt_example: "woman reading on a bench, shot through the leaves, soft green blur"

name: High Selfie Angle
definition: The classic selfie view, with the camera held above the head and tilted down. Big eyes, small chin and an arm reaching just out of frame.
when_to_use: Use for casual phone-style portraits and social media looks. Models may add a stretched arm or a phone, so say no phone visible if you want it hidden.
prompt_example: "high selfie angle of a smiling girl at a summer festival, phone photo"

name: Three-Quarter View
definition: The face or body turned halfway between front and side, so you see both eyes and the curve of the cheek. The classic, most flattering portrait angle.
when_to_use: Use for natural portraits and character art that feels more alive than straight on. For a full side view, use profile shot instead.
prompt_example: "three-quarter view portrait of an old fisherman, window light"

name: Through the Window
definition: Looking at the subject through glass, with reflections, raindrops or a window frame between you. It feels private, quiet and a little cinematic.
when_to_use: Use for cozy, lonely or watching-from-outside moods. Add rain or steam on the glass for extra feeling.
prompt_example: "woman reading in a cafe, seen through the window, rain on glass, night"

name: Reflection Shot
definition: The scene shown in a mirror, puddle, lake or shop window, sometimes upside down or doubled. Instant symmetry and a touch of mystery.
when_to_use: Use for clever compositions and calm, mirrored scenes. Say where the reflection is, like reflected in a puddle, for the best results.
prompt_example: "city lights reflected in a rain puddle, close to the ground, night"

name: Frame Within a Frame
definition: Using a doorway, arch, window or branches to make a natural frame around the subject inside the picture.
when_to_use: Use to pull the eye straight to your subject and add depth. Name the frame, like framed by a stone archway.
prompt_example: "lighthouse framed by a stone archway, golden hour"

name: From Behind
definition: The subject seen from the back, looking out at what they see. It invites you to stand in their shoes.
when_to_use: Use for travel, wonder and quiet, thoughtful moods. Faces stay hidden, which is handy when you do not want a face at all.
prompt_example: "woman seen from behind looking over a misty valley, fog"

name: Johannes Vermeer
definition: (1632-1675) Dutch painter of quiet indoor scenes, often a woman by a window in soft daylight. Pearly light, cool blues and yellows, and calm stillness.
when_to_use: Use for peaceful, softly lit interiors and portraits. Add window light from the left to get his signature look.
prompt_example: "woman pouring milk by a window, in the style of Johannes Vermeer"

name: Rembrandt
definition: (1606-1669) Dutch master of portraits glowing out of deep darkness. Warm golden light, brown shadows and faces full of feeling.
when_to_use: Use for moody, warm portraits lit by one strong light. His name is also a portrait lighting style in photography.
prompt_example: "portrait of an old scholar by candlelight, in the style of Rembrandt"

name: Caravaggio
definition: (1571-1610) Italian painter of dramatic scenes where figures burst out of pitch-black backgrounds in a harsh beam of light. Real, gritty faces and theatrical moments.
when_to_use: Use for intense, dramatic scenes and moody portraits. It is very dark, so it is wrong for bright or cheerful images.
prompt_example: "young musician with a lute lit by a single beam, in the style of Caravaggio"

name: Sandro Botticelli
definition: (c. 1445-1510) Italian Renaissance painter of graceful goddesses with flowing hair, floating fabrics and flower-strewn gardens. Pale, light colors and elegant lines.
when_to_use: Use for romantic, mythical, springtime figures. It shines with flowers and flowing hair, less so with modern scenes.
prompt_example: "goddess with flowing red-gold hair in a flower meadow, in the style of Sandro Botticelli"

name: Jan van Eyck
definition: (c. 1390-1441) Early Flemish painter famous for jewel-bright oil colors and unbelievable detail, down to every bead, fur trim and tiny mirror reflection.
when_to_use: Use for richly detailed portraits and rooms that feel frozen in time. Great with fabrics, jewels and fine textures.
prompt_example: "merchant couple in a candlelit room with a round mirror, in the style of Jan van Eyck"

name: Hieronymus Bosch
definition: (c. 1450-1516) Dutch painter of crowded, strange dream worlds full of tiny creatures, odd machines and giant fruit. Funny, spooky and endlessly weird.
when_to_use: Use for surreal, busy fantasy landscapes packed with little details. Expect chaos, so it is not for simple, clean images.
prompt_example: "crowded fantasy garden with tiny strange creatures and giant strawberries, in the style of Hieronymus Bosch"

name: Albrecht Durer
definition: (1471-1528) German artist best known for incredibly fine engravings and woodcuts, plus careful nature studies like his famous hare. Crisp lines and patient detail.
when_to_use: Use for intricate black ink engravings, old book prints and detailed animal studies. Add the word engraving to get his line work.
prompt_example: "engraving of a knight and a dragon, in the style of Albrecht Durer"

name: Pieter Bruegel the Elder
definition: (c. 1525-1569) Flemish painter of busy village life seen from above: peasant weddings, frozen ponds full of skaters and snowy hunters coming home. Earthy colors and many tiny people.
when_to_use: Use for lively crowd scenes and wintry old village landscapes. Faces are small and simple, so it is not for portraits.
prompt_example: "snowy village with skaters on a frozen pond, in the style of Pieter Bruegel the Elder"

name: Claude Monet
definition: (1840-1926) French Impressionist who painted light more than things: water lilies, haystacks and gardens in soft, dabbed brushstrokes and shimmering color.
when_to_use: Use for dreamy gardens, ponds and sunlit landscapes. Details melt away, so it is not for sharp faces or text.
prompt_example: "water lily pond with a small wooden bridge, in the style of Claude Monet"

name: Vincent van Gogh
definition: (1853-1890) Dutch painter of swirling skies, thick bold brushstrokes and glowing yellows and blues. Everything feels alive and moving.
when_to_use: Use for expressive night skies, sunflowers and countryside scenes full of energy. It is very recognizable, so it can take over a prompt.
prompt_example: "starry night over a sleepy fishing harbor, in the style of Vincent van Gogh"

name: Gustav Klimt
definition: (1862-1918) Austrian painter of dreamy portraits wrapped in gold leaf, swirling patterns and mosaics. Romantic, decorative and shining.
when_to_use: Use for luxurious portraits, lovers and gold patterned backgrounds. Ask for gold leaf to get his famous golden look.
prompt_example: "two lovers embracing in a gold mosaic robe, in the style of Gustav Klimt"

name: Hokusai
definition: (c. 1760-1849) Japanese artist behind The Great Wave, known for woodblock prints with flat bold colors, crisp outlines, deep blues and views of Mount Fuji.
when_to_use: Use for Japanese print-style waves, mountains and everyday scenes. It is a flat print look, so skip it for realism.
prompt_example: "giant wave crashing near a lighthouse, woodblock print, in the style of Hokusai"

name: J.M.W. Turner
definition: (1775-1851) English painter of stormy seas, blazing sunsets and ships lost in golden mist. Light and weather swallow everything.
when_to_use: Use for epic, hazy, glowing skies and wild weather. Shapes dissolve, so do not expect crisp detail.
prompt_example: "ship in a storm at sunset, golden mist, in the style of J.M.W. Turner"

name: Edvard Munch
definition: (1863-1944) Norwegian painter of The Scream, known for wavy, emotional landscapes and figures soaked in anxious feeling. Blood-orange skies and swirling lines.
when_to_use: Use for haunting, emotional, unsettling scenes. It is a heavy mood, not a happy one.
prompt_example: "lonely figure on a bridge under a blood-orange sky, in the style of Edvard Munch"

name: Hilma af Klint
definition: (1862-1944) Swedish painter who made huge, colorful abstract paintings years before abstract art was famous. Spirals, circles, petals and soft pastel symbols.
when_to_use: Use for spiritual, cosmic and geometric abstract art with gentle color. Not for realistic scenes.
prompt_example: "large abstract painting of spirals and petals, pastel pink and blue, in the style of Hilma af Klint"

name: Mary Cassatt
definition: (1844-1926) American Impressionist who lived in Paris and painted tender moments between mothers and children. Soft pastel colors, loose strokes and lots of warmth.
when_to_use: Use for gentle family scenes, quiet portraits and cozy home moments. Best for calm, loving subjects.
prompt_example: "mother bathing a child in a sunny room, in the style of Mary Cassatt"

name: Arthur Rackham
definition: (1867-1939) English illustrator of fairy tales and Peter Pan, full of twisted trees, gnarled roots and tiny fairies. Fine ink lines and faded, earthy watercolor.
when_to_use: Use for spooky but sweet fairy tale scenes and old storybook pages. The colors are muted, so it will not give you bright pops.
prompt_example: "fairies hiding in the roots of a twisted oak, in the style of Arthur Rackham"

name: Alphonse Mucha
definition: (1860-1939) Czech artist of the Art Nouveau poster: graceful women with flowing hair, framed by flowers, halos and curling ornaments in soft colors.
when_to_use: Use for decorative posters, elegant portraits and ornamental borders. Ask for an Art Nouveau poster to get the full frame.
prompt_example: "woman with flowing hair framed by a circle of flowers, Art Nouveau poster, in the style of Alphonse Mucha"

name: Beatrix Potter
definition: (1866-1943) English author and illustrator of Peter Rabbit. Small, gentle watercolors of animals in tiny coats, with real-looking fur and quiet country gardens.
when_to_use: Use for sweet children's book animals and cozy garden scenes. It works best small and simple, not for big epic scenes.
prompt_example: "hedgehog in an apron hanging laundry in a cottage garden, in the style of Beatrix Potter"

name: John Tenniel
definition: (1820-1914) English illustrator who drew the first pictures for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. Crisp black and white engraved lines and odd, slightly stiff characters.
when_to_use: Use for Victorian storybook scenes and curious, Alice-like characters. It is black and white line work, so add color only if you really want it.
prompt_example: "rabbit in a waistcoat checking a pocket watch, in the style of John Tenniel"

name: Edmund Dulac
definition: (1882-1953) French-born British illustrator of fairy tales and the Arabian Nights. Dreamy midnight blues, glowing moons and jewel-like details.
when_to_use: Use for magical night scenes, palaces and starry fairy tales. Lean into deep blue for his classic look.
prompt_example: "princess on a moonlit balcony over a sleeping city, in the style of Edmund Dulac"

name: Aubrey Beardsley
definition: (1872-1898) English illustrator of bold black and white drawings with sweeping curves, big flat black shapes and very fine lines. Elegant, strange and a little wicked.
when_to_use: Use for striking ink posters, decadent portraits and gothic book art. It is pure black and white, so color prompts fight it.
prompt_example: "woman in sweeping peacock-feather robes, black ink, in the style of Aubrey Beardsley"

name: Ivan Bilibin
definition: (1876-1942) Russian illustrator of folk tales, with bold outlines, flat bright colors and fancy patterned borders inspired by old Russian art.
when_to_use: Use for Slavic fairy tales, firebirds and decorated storybook pages. Ask for an ornamental border to get the full page look.
prompt_example: "firebird in a dark forest with ornamental border, in the style of Ivan Bilibin"

name: Harry Clarke
definition: (1889-1931) Irish stained glass artist and illustrator of eerie fairy tales and Edgar Allan Poe stories. Super fine ink detail, jewel patterns and pale, haunting faces.
when_to_use: Use for dark, ornate, spooky illustrations full of tiny detail. Great for gothic stories, less so for cheerful ones.
prompt_example: "pale queen in a jewel-patterned gown, ink illustration, in the style of Harry Clarke"

name: Anime Watercolor Background
definition: Soft hand-painted backgrounds from classic Japanese animated films: see-through watercolor washes, puffy summer clouds, grass that sways and sunlight dappling through leaves.
when_to_use: Use for cozy countryside scenes, nostalgic summer days and any world that should feel gentle and lived-in.
prompt_example: "hillside cottage on a breezy summer afternoon, anime watercolor background, puffy clouds"

name: Anime Light Rays
definition: The glowing light of modern anime films: towering clouds, beams of sun slicing through windows, soft lens glow and tiny floating specks of light, all brighter and cleaner than real life.
when_to_use: Use for hopeful, emotional moments, city skies after rain and anything that should feel like a movie poster for a feeling.
prompt_example: "empty classroom at sunset, anime light rays through the window, floating dust specks"

name: Vaporwave
definition: Internet nostalgia from the 2010s: pink and teal neon, a striped setting sun, a grid floor rolling to the horizon, VHS fuzz and Greek statues in a shopping-mall daydream.
when_to_use: Use for retro-future music art, playful tech nostalgia and anything that should feel like 1987 seen through a dream.
prompt_example: "palm trees and a striped sunset over a neon grid, vaporwave, VHS glitch"

name: Analytic Cubism
definition: Early 1900s painting that breaks people and objects into overlapping see-through shards, showing several sides at once, mostly in browns, greys and muted ochre.
when_to_use: Use for thoughtful, puzzle-like portraits and still lifes, or to show one subject from many angles at once.
prompt_example: "cafe table with a guitar and a newspaper, analytic cubism, muted browns and greys"

name: Henri Matisse
definition: (1869-1954) French painter who, late in life, made bright paper cut-outs: shapes snipped from hand-painted paper, seaweed forms, stars and dancers in pure, joyful color.
when_to_use: Use for bold, cheerful compositions with simple shapes, posters and anything that should feel like a celebration.
prompt_example: "swimmers among seaweed shapes, in the style of Henri Matisse paper cut-outs"

name: Flat Vector Illustration
definition: Today's clean digital illustration: solid color shapes with no outlines, a soft grain texture, friendly characters in expressive poses and plenty of breathing room.
when_to_use: Use for explainers, app and brand graphics, editorial spots and characters that should feel modern and approachable.
prompt_example: "woman watering plants on a sunny balcony, flat vector illustration, soft grain texture"

name: Bauhaus Graphic Design
definition: The 1920s German design school look: circles, squares and triangles in red, yellow, blue and black, strong grids and clean sans-serif lettering.
when_to_use: Use for posters, logos and layouts that should feel smart, modern and built with a ruler.
prompt_example: "exhibition poster of a cat made of circles and triangles, bauhaus graphic design, red yellow blue"

name: Early CGI
definition: The look of 1990s computer graphics: shiny plastic surfaces, chrome balls, checkerboard floors with perfect reflections and a slightly toy-like, too-clean finish.
when_to_use: Use for retro tech nostalgia, music-video throwbacks and playful 3D scenes that wink at the dawn of computer art.
prompt_example: "chrome sphere on a checkerboard floor, early cgi, 1993 render"

name: Cave Painting
definition: The oldest art we know: animals drawn in red ochre and charcoal on rough rock walls, stencilled handprints, and flickering firelight bringing it all to life.
when_to_use: Use for ancient, primal moods, origin stories and any subject that should feel timeless and deeply human.
prompt_example: "herd of horses running across a rock wall, cave painting, red ochre and charcoal"

name: Egyptian Tomb Painting
definition: Ancient Egyptian wall art: figures with side-on faces and front-facing eyes, flat bright colors, crisp outlines and rows of hieroglyphs in neat bands.
when_to_use: Use for stylized storytelling scenes, mythic portraits and any subject that should feel ceremonial and ancient.
prompt_example: "cat sipping tea at a low table, egyptian tomb painting, hieroglyph border"

name: Dunhuang Mural
definition: Buddhist cave paintings from the Silk Road in China: earthy red backgrounds, mineral greens and blues, flying celestial figures trailing long ribbons, and paint worn and flaking with age.
when_to_use: Use for graceful, spiritual scenes, flowing fabric and anything that should feel ancient, sacred and softly faded.
prompt_example: "celestial dancer with flowing ribbons, dunhuang mural, faded mineral colors"

name: Infinity Polka Dots
definition: Dots everywhere: bold polka dots covering walls, floors, objects and people until everything melts into one endless pattern, often red and white or yellow and black.
when_to_use: Use for immersive, playful installation scenes, statement fashion and dreamy rooms that feel like they go on forever.
prompt_example: "room covered in red polka dots with mirrored walls, infinity polka dots"

name: Surrealism
definition: Dream logic painted with realistic detail: melting clocks, impossible deserts, long shadows and ordinary objects behaving in ways that make no sense.
when_to_use: Use for dreams, strange feelings and ideas you can't show literally.
prompt_example: "melting pocket watch draped over a tree branch in a desert at dusk, surrealism"

name: American Realism
definition: Quiet American scenes from the 1920s to the 1950s: diners, hotel rooms and city windows with hard-edged sunlight, flat shadows and people lost in their own thoughts.
when_to_use: Use for lonely, reflective moments, urban stillness and stories told in a single look out of a window.
prompt_example: "woman by a window in morning sun, american realism, hard light across an empty room"

name: Silver Age Comics
definition: Comic books from the late 1950s to about 1970: cosmic heroes, blocky muscular action, crackling energy dots, big sound-effect lettering and four-color printing.
when_to_use: Use for explosive action, sci-fi heroes and anything that needs a loud, joyful comic-book bang.
prompt_example: "hero bursting through a wall, silver age comics, crackling energy dots, KRAKOOM lettering"

name: Pop Line Figures
definition: Simple figures drawn with thick, even black lines and flat bright colors, surrounded by little radiating motion lines so they look like they're dancing or buzzing.
when_to_use: Use for upbeat murals, music and party graphics, and any message about energy, love or togetherness.
prompt_example: "crowd of dancing figures with motion lines, pop line figures, bold black outlines, yellow background"

name: Chinese Shadow Puppetry
definition: Translucent leather puppets lit from behind a paper screen: lace-like cut patterns, glowing color, jointed limbs moved on rods and the warm flicker of an oil lamp.
when_to_use: Use for folk tales, theatrical storytelling and scenes that should feel handmade, warm and ancient.
prompt_example: "warrior and dragon behind a glowing paper screen, chinese shadow puppetry, translucent leather"

name: Math Morph Explainer
definition: The calm style of popular math videos: a dark background, one idea on screen at a time, and shapes that smoothly morph from one concept into the next, with each idea keeping its own color.
when_to_use: Use when explaining how something works step by step, like an equation, an algorithm or how an AI model learns.
prompt_example: "dark background, a glowing curve smoothly morphs into a bar chart, math explainer animation"

name: Data Chart Animation
definition: The newsroom way to animate numbers: the axes draw in first, then the data grows into place, and only one thing gets highlighted. Bars start at zero, one color for the star, grey for the rest.
when_to_use: Use for any number you want people to remember, like growth, price changes or before-and-after comparisons.
prompt_example: "bar chart grows up from zero, one bar highlighted in red, clean finance chart animation"

name: Keynote Reveal
definition: Product-launch presentation style: one idea per screen, a soft glowing background, frosted-glass cards and big numbers that land the moment they're mentioned.
when_to_use: Use for software tutorials, feature announcements and showing off a product or a result.
prompt_example: "giant number 8 fades up on a dark navy background, frosted glass card, product keynote style"

name: Whiteboard Animation
definition: A hand-drawn explainer where a pen sketches simple pictures, arrows and words on a board while the narrator talks, then pulls back to show the whole idea as one map.
when_to_use: Use to explain processes, relationships and step-by-step ideas alongside a voiceover.
prompt_example: "marker draws a clock, an arrow and a lightbulb on a chalkboard, whiteboard animation"

name: Collage Explainer
definition: The investigative news-video look: real clippings, photos and charts laid on a desk, with red lines and highlighter drawn on as the camera moves from clue to clue.
when_to_use: Use for arguments built on evidence, like news stories, history and how-it-really-happened breakdowns.
prompt_example: "newspaper clippings and a chart on a desk, red marker circles the key number, collage explainer"

name: Flat Science Explainer
definition: Bright flat shapes with no outlines in a softly glowing world, where the camera zooms between the tiny and the enormous, from a single cell to a whole planet.
when_to_use: Use for science, space, biology and big-picture ideas where scale is the story.
prompt_example: "camera zooms from a drop of seawater into a glowing diatom, flat science explainer, no outlines"

name: Kinetic Typography
definition: Words are the actors: the key word slams onto the screen on the beat, supporting words slide up from below, and there's only ever one thing to read at a time.
when_to_use: Use for openers, quotes, lists and short-form video where the words carry the message.
prompt_example: "the word AGENTS slams onto a black screen in bold yellow, kinetic typography"

name: Storytime Animation
definition: The story-channel cartoon: a simple character with thick outlines snaps between a few poses, cuts to a big reaction close-up and holds still for the punchline.
when_to_use: Use for personal stories, funny mishaps and talking-to-camera content where the voice is the star.
prompt_example: "cartoon girl with big glasses shrugs at a computer full of code, storytime animation, thick outlines"
